findings.claim: The encounter ledger enforces one clinical rule at the write path that a shadow scorer cannot bypass: a model output must arrive with an uncertainty estimate carrying a 'coverage' key, or the write raises MissingUncertainty. Only model=='event' is exempt.
findings.evidence: backend/services/encounter_ledger.py:253-265 `def _check_uncertainty(model, uncertainty): if model == _EVENT_MODEL: return; if not uncertainty: raise MissingUncertainty(...); if "coverage" not in uncertainty: raise MissingUncertainty("...a prediction set with no stated coverage is not a calibrated claim")`; :60 `_EVENT_MODEL = "event"`

findings.claim: The ledger raises LedgerUnavailable rather than swallowing a failed write, and refine_triage currently catches it and continues — justified there because the score is already in front of the clinician. In a shadow programme that justification inverts: the ledger entry IS the product, so a swallowed failure means the week-14 report silently under-counts.
findings.evidence: backend/services/encounter_ledger.py:102-109 `class LedgerUnavailable(RuntimeError): """...A ledger that drops writes quietly is worse than no ledger at all: the gap reads as 'nothing happened to this patient' rather than 'we failed to write it down'..."""`; backend/routers/triage.py:114-118 `except encounter_ledger.LedgerUnavailable: ... log.exception("could not append refined triage to the encounter ledger")`

findings.claim: The ledger's sequence allocator retries at most 8 times on contention and then raises. At a <=5-minute cadence one writer per encounter this is ample, but a design that fans out concurrent scorers onto the same encounter_id would consume attempts against itself.
findings.evidence: backend/services/encounter_ledger.py:115 `_MAX_SEQ_ATTEMPTS = 8`; :303-340 the retry loop, ending `raise LedgerUnavailable(f"could not allocate a sequence number for encounter {encounter_id!r} after {_MAX_SEQ_ATTEMPTS} attempts")`; backend/tests/services/test_encounter_ledger_durability.py:160-166 `test_a_writer_gives_up_rather_than_spinning`

findings.claim: The ledger reads through to DynamoDB on a cold module cache specifically so a fresh Lambda container does not restart numbering at 1 and write a second unlinked chain over the real one. Any scheduler running in a new container per invocation depends on this path working.
findings.evidence: backend/services/encounter_ledger.py:206-217 `def _chain(encounter_id): """A Lambda container that never saw this encounter has an empty dict and a full table. Without this read-through it would start numbering at 1 again and write a second, unlinked chain over the top of the real one.""" chain = _entries.get(encounter_id); if chain is None: chain = _load_all(encounter_id)`

findings.claim: SEC-002's redaction filter only catches three shapes: a UUID4 with hyphens, 'Bearer <token>', and 'intake_token=<token>'. Patient ids in this codebase are frequently NOT UUID4-shaped (pt-<hex>), so those go to CloudWatch intact. Names, chief complaints, vitals, ESI levels and hospital_id are never redacted by this mechanism at all.
findings.evidence: backend/lib/log_redaction.py:19-25 `_UUID_RX = re.compile(r"\b[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-...")`, `_BEARER_RX`, `_NONCE_RX` — and nothing else; :38 `if not any(rx.search(msg) for rx in (_UUID_RX, _BEARER_RX, _NONCE_RX)): return True`. Non-UUID ids in use: backend/tests/test_tenant_isolation.py:52 `pid = f"pt-beta-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"`, backend/tests/test_public_endpoint_throttling.py:189 `pid = f"pt-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}"`

findings.claim: Redaction is installed by an explicit call in main.py, and it works by attaching to HANDLERS plus monkeypatching Logger.addHandler so handlers attached later (uvicorn, the Lambda runtime) are also covered. A separate scheduler entrypoint that does not import main gets no redaction whatsoever.
findings.evidence: backend/main.py:32-34 `from lib import log_redaction  # noqa: E402` / `log_redaction.install()`; backend/lib/log_redaction.py:59-90 `"Filters go on HANDLERS, not on loggers, and that distinction is the whole point of this function."`; :92-100 `logging.Logger.addHandler = add_handler` with the reason `"uvicorn and the Lambda runtime install their handlers at times we do not control"`

findings.claim: There is an existing, tested pattern for what a background writer logs when it cannot record something: name the action and the status, never the item. audit.py deliberately omits the patient id from its loudest error line, and a test asserts the id does not appear.
findings.evidence: backend/lib/audit.py:83-90 `# Deliberately names the action and not the item. The patient id is what would make this line useful and is exactly what SEC-002 keeps out of CloudWatch` / `log.error("AUDIT RECORD LOST: action=%s status=%s...", item.get("action"), item.get("status_code"), _write_failures)`; backend/tests/test_audit_and_lockout_integrity.py:81-94 `test_the_failure_log_carries_no_patient_identifier` asserts `"3f2504e0" not in blob`

findings.claim: lib/tenancy.py logs a patient_id at WARNING on every cross-tenant refusal. That id survives redaction unless it happens to be UUID4-shaped, so this is an existing SEC-002 leak that a background job iterating patients would amplify if it reuses require_patient with a mismatched hospital.
findings.evidence: backend/lib/tenancy.py:53-56 `log.warning("cross-tenant patient access refused: hospital=%s patient=%s", hospital_id, patient_id)`

findings.claim: SEC-003 derives the public surface by AST-walking routers/*.py: a handler is any FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef with an ast.Call decorator whose func is an ast.Attribute in {get,post,put,patch,delete}; auth is classified by substring hints over ast.unparse(node.args)+ast.unparse(node.decorator_list); the behaviour of interest is classified by marker substrings over ast.unparse(node). The obligation list is then parametrized, with a keyed exemption dict, a staleness test, and a floor assertion. This is the mechanical template a shadow-guarantee test should copy.
findings.evidence: backend/tests/test_public_endpoint_throttling.py:78-105 `_public_routes()`; :47-50 `_AUTH_HINTS`; :54-59 `_PATIENT_DATA`; :63-75 `ALLOWED_UNTHROTTLED: dict[str, str]`; :109-113 `NEEDS_THROTTLE`; :121-132 the parametrized rule; :135-138 `test_exemptions_still_match_real_routes`; :116-118 `test_the_route_scan_found_the_public_surface` asserting `len(PUBLIC_ROUTES) >= 20`

findings.claim: SEC-004 adds two ideas SEC-003 lacks and both are needed for the shadow test: a fixed-point import closure with absorbing 'gated boundary' nodes, and a tripwire test that re-derives the leaf set from call signatures with docstrings blanked, so prose about a mechanism cannot masquerade as the mechanism.
findings.evidence: backend/tests/services/test_consent_gate.py:145-164 `_reaches_provider()` with `if deps & (reached - GATED_BOUNDARIES)`; :221-241 `test_provider_leaves_are_still_the_only_leaves` — `for node in ast.walk(tree): # blank out docstrings so prose cannot match` then `if any(c in ast.unparse(tree) for c in calls): found.add(name)` and `assert not (found - PROVIDER_LEAVES)`

findings.claim: Both derived-scope tests pair static analysis with DRIVING the behaviour, on the stated principle that a cited line proves code was written, not that it covers the claim. SEC-003 fires 25 real requests at the SMS route; SEC-008 issues a real JWT and reads a real cross-tenant note. A shadow-guarantee test that is static-only would be exactly the failure mode the constitution's preamble describes.
findings.evidence: backend/tests/test_public_endpoint_throttling.py:199-207 `statuses = [client.post("/api/demo/sms/care-instructions", ...).status_code for _ in range(25)]; assert 429 in statuses`; backend/tests/test_tenant_isolation.py:86-94 `r = alpha_client.get(f"/api/{ALPHA}/patients/{beta_patient}/notes"); assert r.status_code == 404; assert "HIV+" not in r.text`; CONSTITUTION.md:24-27

findings.claim: The append-only guarantee is already enforced by a name-scan over the module's public surface, restated a second time after the storage layer was added. This is the cheapest precedent for the 'no egress' assertion: enumerate the surface, intersect with a forbidden set, assert empty.
findings.evidence: backend/tests/services/test_encounter_ledger.py:143-148 `forbidden = {"update","delete","remove","edit","amend","overwrite","pop"}; exposed = {n for n in dir(el) if not n.startswith("_")}; assert not (forbidden & exposed)`; backend/tests/services/test_encounter_ledger_durability.py:178-183 the same check re-stated with `{"modify","set","put","save"}` added, docstring `"that is exactly when an innocent-looking save or put tends to appear"`

findings.claim: test_dev_echo_is_never_deployed.py establishes the pattern for a control that must hold regardless of configuration: the dangerous setting is forced inert inside a deployed environment (detected by AWS_LAMBDA_FUNCTION_NAME et al), logged at error rather than crashing the app, and a test asserts main.py actually calls the hardening function because 'a guard nothing calls is decoration'. A SHADOW_MODE that disables egress should be built this way, not as a flag anyone can flip.
findings.evidence: backend/tests/test_dev_echo_is_never_deployed.py:34-38 the env fixture deleting `AWS_LAMBDA_FUNCTION_NAME`, `AWS_EXECUTION_ENV`, `AWS_LAMBDA_RUNTIME_API`; :96-102 `test_hardening_runs_at_startup` — `assert "harden_for_deployment()" in main, "main.py never calls harden_for_deployment(), so the guard never runs"`; backend/lib/config.py:159-166 `if is_deployed() and settings.email_dev_echo: object.__setattr__(settings, "email_dev_echo", False); log.error(...)`; :148-154 `"A comment saying MUST is not a control."`

findings.claim: ARCH-002 (L1) says only db/ modules initialize boto3 clients, and services/ already violates it in eleven places — including services/encounter_ledger.py, the module the shadow programme is built on, and services/triage_ml.py, the scorer. A scheduler that follows the existing ledger pattern inherits an L1 violation; one that follows ARCH-002 has to route ledger persistence through db/.
findings.evidence: CONSTITUTION.md:328-334 `ARCH-002 ... level: L1 / check: Services may import db.storage; only db/ modules initialize boto3 clients. / scope: backend/services/*.py`. Violations: backend/services/encounter_ledger.py:125-129 `import boto3 ... return boto3.resource("dynamodb", ...).Table(LEDGER_TABLE)`; backend/services/triage_ml.py:45-47 `import boto3 ... s3 = boto3.client("s3", ...)`; also services/transcription.py:136-147, services/tts.py:184-186, services/email.py:50-52, services/sms.py:303-306, services/ambient_scribe.py:390,415, services/workflows/storage.py:28-29, services/voice_agent/session.py:200-201, services/voice_agent/tts_cache.py:79-81,139-140

findings.claim: Two of the rules the task brief flagged as critical are L2, not L1: PERF-004 (no .scan() in hot paths) and SEC-008 (clinician JWT + hospital_id match). PERF-004's written scope is only triage/intake/patients routers. There is no .scan() anywhere in routers/, services/, db/ or lib/ today — every '.scan(' hit is content_guard.scan or ehr_copilot.scan.
findings.evidence: CONSTITUTION.md:771-778 `PERF-004 ... level: L2 ... scope: backend/routers/triage.py, backend/routers/intake.py, backend/routers/patients.py`; CONSTITUTION.md:146-152 `SEC-008 ... level: L2`. `grep -rn "\.scan(" backend/routers backend/services backend/db backend/lib` returns only content_guard.scan / ehr_copilot.scan call sites.

findings.claim: COMP-005 (L1) names bedrock as the default Claude provider, but the deploy script ships CLAUDE_PROVIDER=direct to the production Lambda. This matters for the shadow design only as a boundary condition: it is one more reason the shadow scorer must not reach an AI provider at all.
findings.evidence: CONSTITUTION.md:232-238 `COMP-005 ... level: L1 / check: CLAUDE_PROVIDER=bedrock, TRANSCRIPTION_PROVIDER=aws, TTS_PROVIDER=aws are defaults; direct third-party APIs are opt-in fallback only`; scripts/deploy_container.py:111 `"CLAUDE_PROVIDER": "direct",  # flip to "bedrock" after AWS BAA + model access`

findings.claim: triage_ml.model_version() exists specifically because the ledger refuses an unversioned entry, and it returns (version, how_it_was_derived) so the ledger can record whether the version was declared by the artifacts or is a content hash. It returns 'no-artifacts'/'absent' when nothing loads — meaning a shadow job running on a container with missing artifacts would still produce writable-looking entries unless it checks.
findings.evidence: backend/services/triage_ml.py:552-586 `def model_version() -> tuple[str, str]: ... if art is None: return "no-artifacts", "absent" ... if declared: return str(declared), "declared" ... return f"sha256:{digest}", "content_hash"`; used at backend/routers/triage.py:88 `model_version, version_source = triage_ml.model_version()` and recorded at :111 `"model_version_source": version_source`

hard_constraints: The scheduled re-score MUST NOT be delivered as a plain EventBridge event to the existing solace-api Lambda handler. backend/main.py:266 short-circuits on `event.get("source") == "aws.events"` and returns a 200 warmup body without dispatching. PERF-002 (L1) requires that branch to exist, so it cannot be removed. Either (a) use a separate function with its own handler, or (b) discriminate on a field the warmup branch does not consume and reorder the checks so the re-score branch is tested FIRST — and add a test that asserts a re-score event does not return {"warm": true}, because that failure is silent and reports success.

Whatever function receives the schedule MUST have its async invoke config pinned to MaximumRetryAttempts=0 and a short MaximumEventAge IN CODE, in scripts/deploy_container.py (or an equivalent script), not by hand in the console. The current script deletes and recreates the function on every deploy and never sets EventInvokeConfig, so the exact retry amplification from 42abe22 (360 pings -> 1,080 invocations) returns on the next deploy. This is the specific way this project has already lost money once.

The re-score path MUST carry a hard time budget of the same shape as _run_warmup: work on a joined thread with a timeout, not a deadline checked between steps. 42abe22 records that the between-steps version was tried first and was useless, because the call that hung was _load() and it never returned to be checked (backend/main.py:208-222, backend/tests/test_warmup_is_bounded.py:49-65). A per-patient budget AND a per-invocation budget are both needed, since the loop length is the department census.

The job MUST NOT call storage.update_patient / storage.put_patient with any scoring field. refined_esi_level is projected by routers/patients.py:46-48,101-107 and PatientCard.tsx:20-22 displays it in preference to esi_level. Writing the patient row is writing the ED board. The ledger is the only write target the shadow guarantee permits.

The job MUST NOT call services.workflows.engine.fire(). One call reaches send_sms, send_slack_webhook, http_webhook, create_clinician_note, set_patient_field, ehr_write and notify (services/workflows/actions.py:375-520). refine_triage does call fire() at routers/triage.py:121-136, so the shadow scorer must not be built by copying refine_triage's body.

The job MUST NOT expose a route. SEC-003's scope is 'derived from the route table — any handler with no auth dependency' (CONSTITUTION.md:71); adding a shadow read endpoint would pull it into SEC-003 and into the public surface. During the 90 days the ledger's existing reader endpoints (routers/encounters.py:56, :83) are clinician-authenticated and would surface a shadow score to a clinician on request — either shadow encounters must be excluded from them or those routes must be off for the shadow cohort.

Iteration MUST be per-hospital and driven by an explicit hospital_id, via storage.list_patients_for_hospital(hospital_id, ...). There is no cross-tenant enumeration primitive today and none must be added; a `list_all_patients` helper would create the SEC-008 violation that does not currently exist. Every ledger write must be preceded by a tenancy check on the loaded row (tenancy.belongs_to(row, hospital_id), lib/tenancy.py:62-71) rather than trusting the GSI query.

Iteration MUST paginate. _ddb_query_patients_by_hospital (db/storage.py:181-187) does not handle LastEvaluatedKey. Silently scoring only the first 1 MB page of a department is a correctness failure that the week-14 under-triage number would absorb without any error surfacing.

The ledger entry MUST carry hospital_id, or the week-14 analysis cannot scope its own evidence. Today the item has no tenant column (encounter_ledger.py:148-163) and the table has no GSI (setup_aws.py:170-180), while tenancy on the read path is borrowed from a patient row that is TTL'd 30 minutes after the patient is marked seen (routers/patients.py:190-200). Adding hospital_id to the item changes the hash payload in _digest (encounter_ledger.py:234-249) and therefore breaks verification of any chain written before the change — so it must be decided BEFORE the programme starts, not during it.

The programme MUST retain an enumerable index of its own encounter_ids outside the patients table. The ledger allow grants PutItem/GetItem/Query only, no Scan (scripts/iam_ledger_allow.json), and the ledger has no GSI, so at week 14 there is no way to ask 'which encounters exist'. Widening the IAM allow to add Scan would trip test_ledger_iam_policy.py:110-115.

A ledger write failure MUST NOT be swallowed. routers/triage.py:114-118 catches LedgerUnavailable and continues, correctly, because the score is already in front of the clinician. In the shadow programme the ledger entry IS the entire product, so the failure must be surfaced and counted (the audit module's _write_failures + /health pattern at lib/audit.py:41-50 and main.py:100-110 is the in-repo precedent), not logged and dropped.

Every ledger entry MUST carry an uncertainty dict containing a 'coverage' key or the write raises MissingUncertainty (encounter_ledger.py:253-265), and MUST carry a model_version, obtained from triage_ml.model_version() which also reports whether the version was declared or content-hashed (triage_ml.py:552-586). observed_at must be timezone-aware or record() raises (encounter_ledger.py:292-296).

Audit writes from the job MUST be synchronous, or explicitly drained before the handler returns. lib/audit.py:156-160 dispatches to the default asyncio executor and returns; Lambda freezes the container the instant the handler returns, so queued audit rows are lost with no error. The job should call the synchronous path or await completion.
Audit action names MUST NOT begin with 'abuse.' unless abuse is meant. lib/audit.py:170-184 auto-increments the blocklist for any action with that prefix.

The job MUST log neither patient identifiers nor clinical content. lib/log_redaction.py only redacts hyphenated UUID4, 'Bearer <tok>' and 'intake_token=<tok>' — not pt-<hex> ids, names, complaints, vitals or ESI values. If the scheduler runs as a separate entrypoint it MUST call log_redaction.install() as its first act, since backend/main.py:34 is the only thing that installs it today and a handler that does not import main gets nothing. Follow the audit.py:83-90 pattern: log the action and the count, never the item.

Whether a consent gate is required MUST be decided explicitly and written down, because neither SEC-004's derived scope nor its test reaches this path (triage_ml is outside the provider closure; the rule only obliges unauthenticated ROUTES). If the answer is 'yes', the mechanism already exists: consent.for_patient(patient) at lib/consent.py:89-98, gated once at a single choke point in the scorer with a test that calls it and asserts refusal — the services.workflows.actions.run pattern (test_consent_gate.py:62-64, :407-419), not a per-call-site check.

The job MUST NOT reach any of the four provider leaves (services.transcription, services.tts, lib.claude, services.voice_agent.tts_cache). Doing so would pull it into SEC-004's derived scope, and would additionally engage SEC-005 (L1, content_guard.scan before submission), COMP-001 (L1, Safe Harbor redaction) and COMP-005 (L1, BAA-covered provider — the deployed function currently ships CLAUDE_PROVIDER=direct, scripts/deploy_container.py:111).

Model loading MUST go through triage_ml._load() and its @lru_cache(maxsize=1). PERF-001 (L1) and ARCH-004 (L2) both require it, and the warmup path depends on it being the same cached load (CONSTITUTION.md:737-746, 351-360). A per-invocation model load in a 5-minute loop is also the cost shape that caused the original incident.

Any boto3 the job needs MUST live in db/, per ARCH-002 (L1, CONSTITUTION.md:328-334). services/ already violates this in eleven places including encounter_ledger.py:125-129 — the design should not add a twelfth by putting the scheduler's persistence in services/.

The shadow guarantee MUST be enforced by a derived-scope test whose allowlist is EMPTY, not by review. The product promise is 'no code path exists', so any entry in an ALLOWED_EGRESS dict is the promise being weakened and must be defended in writing — mirroring ALLOWED_UNGATED (test_consent_gate.py:74-109) and ALLOWED_UNTHROTTLED (test_public_endpoint_throttling.py:63-75), each paired with a staleness test and a floor assertion so a scan that matches nothing cannot pass vacuously (test_consent_gate.py:211-219).
unknowns: THE SHADOW GUARANTEE TEST — concrete design, since this is the deliverable the brief asked for and it does not exist yet. Proposed file: backend/tests/test_shadow_has_no_egress.py, rule SHADOW-001 (L1). (1) DERIVE THE EGRESS LEAVES rather than listing them, using the docstring-blanking trick from test_consent_gate.py:221-241: ast.parse every first-party module, blank every ast.Expr/ast.Constant string so prose cannot match, ast.unparse, and match call signatures for each egress mechanism — HTTP response (any FunctionDef carrying an ast.Call decorator whose func is an ast.Attribute in {get,post,put,patch,delete}, i.e. SEC-003's exact route detector at test_public_endpoint_throttling.py:87-91); patient-row writes ('storage.update_patient(', 'storage.put_patient('); notes ('storage.add_note('); messaging ('sms.send(', 'send_email(', 'boto3.client(\"sns'); webhooks ('httpx.', 'requests.'); EHR write-back ('services.fhir_writer', 'services.ehr_gateway', 'services.hl7_v2', 'ehr_writeback_queue'); and the workflow fan-out ('workflows.engine.fire(', 'engine.fire(') — fire() is a single leaf standing for seven actions (services/workflows/actions.py:375-520). Assert the derived leaf set is a superset of a small hand floor so a broken matcher cannot pass empty, and assert no NEW module matches an egress signature without being declared, exactly as test_provider_leaves_are_still_the_only_leaves does. (2) COMPUTE THE SHADOW CLOSURE by running the SEC-004 fixed point FORWARD from one declared root: build the same edges map as test_consent_gate.py:118-142 (_source_modules + _import_edges), seed reachable={'services.shadow_scorer'}, and repeatedly add every first-party dep of every member until stable. (3) ASSERT reachable ∩ EGRESS_LEAVES == set(), with ALLOWED_EGRESS: dict[str,str] keyed 'module:leaf' whose correct steady state is EMPTY, plus a test_exemptions_still_correspond_to_real_edges killing stale entries. (4) ASSERT THE WRITE ALLOWLIST — closure proves unreachability, not that the writes it does make are the right ones. AST-walk the shadow package for every attribute call and assert the set of qualified callee names ⊆ {encounter_ledger.record, audit.record, storage.get_patient, storage.list_patients_for_hospital, triage_ml.predict, triage_ml.model_version, consent.for_patient, tenancy.belongs_to} — read-only on the patient store, append-only on the ledger. This is the assertion that catches the specific trap that writing refined_esi_level is writing the ED board. (5) ASSERT NO ROUTE: no FunctionDef in the shadow package carries a verb decorator, and main.py contains no include_router for the shadow package. (6) DRIVE IT, because both existing derived-scope tests do and the preamble says a cited line proves nothing: in local mode, seed one patient, monkeypatch spies onto storage.update_patient, storage.put_patient, storage.add_note, sms.send, email.send_email, httpx.Client.post, workflows.engine.fire and lib.claude.messages_create, run exactly one scoring pass, assert every spy has zero calls, and assert encounter_ledger.timeline(pid) gained exactly one entry with verify(pid).ok is True. (7) FLOOR ASSERTIONS on len(SHADOW_MODULES) and on the leaf set. I could not implement or verify this because the scorer module does not exist yet — the root name is the one thing the design must fix before the test can be written.

The legal basis for the shadow programme — treatment and operations, quality improvement, or research under IRB — is not determinable from the code, and it decides whether a consent gate is required at all. The constitution defers the structurally identical voice question to the deploying hospital's counsel (CONSTITUTION.md:108-111) and ships VOICE_CONSENT_MODE as a setting rather than picking an answer. The same shape is probably right here, but the code cannot answer it.

How patients enter the system for the shadow programme is entirely unspecified in code. routers/intake.py:302 is the only caller of storage.put_patient, so today a patient row exists only if that patient completed Solace's own intake. 'Re-score EVERY patient currently in the department' implies an EHR-driven census that has no ingestion path, no consent_granted_at, and therefore no row for consent.for_patient() to read. I could not determine whether the design intends to create shadow patient rows, to key the ledger off an EHR encounter id instead, or something else — and this choice determines almost every other answer above.

Whether the solace-warmer EventBridge rule is currently enabled or disabled in AWS. 42abe22 says it was disabled, but that state lives only in AWS; scripts/deploy_container.py:157-171 re-points it on every deploy regardless. I ran no AWS calls (read-only investigation, no credentials used).

The actual size of the patient set per hospital, so I cannot say whether the un-paginated GSI query in _ddb_query_patients_by_hospital would exceed the 1 MB page today. The defect is real regardless; only its current blast radius is unknown.

Whether triage_ml.predict() is safe to call repeatedly on a patient with no measured vitals. refine_triage requires a VitalsBody and raises 400 when body is None (routers/triage.py:57-58), and the warmup path constructs a full synthetic vitals dict (main.py:236-246). A continuous re-scorer over a whole department will frequently have partial or absent vitals, and I did not read predict()'s imputation behaviour far enough to say what it returns or whether the conformal coverage figure remains meaningful under heavy missingness. The strategy doc's own acceptance bar says the estimate must 'refuse to emit when input completeness is below a stated threshold' (docs/strategy/2026-07-30-product-strategy.md:302), and I found no such threshold in the code.

Whether the S3 audit archive is actually configured in production. lib/audit.py:99-100 silently returns without archiving when solace_mode != 'aws' or s3_bucket_media is unset, which would leave only the 90-day DynamoDB TTL against COMP-002's 6-year requirement. Determining this needs AWS access.

Whether adding hospital_id to the ledger item is acceptable mid-flight. It enters _digest's payload (encounter_ledger.py:234-249), so every pre-existing chain would fail verify() after the change. I could not determine whether any production ledger entries exist yet.

designs.name: Shadow Tick — one dedicated Lambda, one disabled-by-default EventBridge rule, one roster table
designs.summary:
A single `rate(5 minutes)` EventBridge rule invokes ONE dedicated Lambda function (`solace-shadow`), built from the SAME container image as `solace-api` with `ImageConfig.Command = ["shadow.handler"]`. One invocation = one "tick" that loops the whole department in-process. No per-patient fan-out, no Step Functions, no Fargate, no queues.

I broke my own minimum-moving-parts prior in exactly three places, and each one buys something a shared resource cannot:

1. A SECOND LAMBDA rather than a branch in `main.handler`. A new branch before the warmup check at `backend/main.py:266` would work and would not violate PERF-002 (the warmup branch stays intact, `{"warmup":true}` still routes to it, the deploy smoke test at `scripts/deploy_container.py:174-184` still passes). I rejected it anyway for one reason: you cannot set `ReservedConcurrentExecutions` on the scheduler without also capping the clinician API. Reserved concurrency is the only control that makes a 42abe22 repeat *physically impossible* rather than merely unlikely, and this team found the last incident by reading an invoice. A second function from the same image costs one `create_function` call and one log group. It also gives an Errors alarm that means something (the shared `solace-lambda-errors` alarm at `scripts/setup_cloudwatch_alarms.py:48-54` fires at >5 per 5 min; the incident ran at ~3.75 and hid for weeks), an independent timeout, and — for requirement 6 — a separate execution role with NO write permission on `solace-patients`, which turns "no code path to the ED board" from a promise into an IAM boundary.

2. A NEW TABLE `solace-shadow-roster` (PK `hospital_id` S, SK `state#encounter_id` S). It earns its place three times: (a) enumeration by `Query(hospital_id = :h AND begins_with(sk, "open#"))` — a key condition, not a filter, so it reads only open encounters and never degrades as 10,800 closed ones accumulate; (b) it is the durable `encounter_id -> hospital_id` map that outlives the patient row, which is what makes the week-14 join computable at all; (c) it snapshots the immutable scoring inputs (transcript, medical_info, language) at enrolment, so the 24h/30-minute patient TTL cannot destroy the ability to re-score mid-stay. Because the roster carries tenancy, I do NOT add `hospital_id` to the ledger item — which avoids touching `_digest` (`encounter_ledger.py:234-249`), avoids invalidating every pre-existing chain, avoids a ledger GSI, and avoids amending `scripts/iam_ledger_allow.json` and breaking `backend/tests/test_ledger_iam_policy.py:110-116`. One boring PAY_PER_REQUEST table at ~300 reads/day pages nobody.

3. A SEPARATE IAM ROLE `solace-shadow-exec`, with an explicit `Deny` on `dynamodb:PutItem`, `UpdateItem`, `DeleteItem` for `table/solace-patients`. Requirement 6 stops being a review item.

Everything else reuses what exists. The tick calls `triage_ml.predict()` (pure local LightGBM, zero network, outside SEC-004's derived provider closure), applies the raise-only floor from `triage_rules.evaluate()`, and appends to `encounter_ledger`. It never calls `storage.update_patient`, never calls `workflows.engine.fire()`, and exposes no HTTP route.

The tick body:
  budget = min(45.0, remaining_ms/1000 - 15)      # function Timeout=120
  tick_id = floor(epoch_now / 300)                 # derived from the clock, not the event
  guard: solace_mode == "aws"; PROGRAMME_START <= now <= PROGRAMME_END
  for each hospital in settings.shadow_hospital_ids:
     enrol:   Query patients GSI hospital_id=:h AND created_at > :cursor  (paginated) -> conditional PutItem per new encounter, advance cursor
     enumerate: Query roster begins_with(sk,"open#")  (paginated)
     for each open encounter, while monotonic() < deadline:
        tail = encounter_ledger.tail(eid)                       # 1 item
        if tail and tail.output.get("tick_id") >= tick_id: continue      # idempotent
        if tail_tick_id < tick_id - 1: record cadence_gap event          # req 3
        score on a daemon thread joined with an 8s timeout               # 42abe22 pattern
        record ONE entry, then update the roster
     record heartbeat entry; audit "shadow.tick"; return a summary dict (never raises)
designs.trigger_mechanism:
One classic EventBridge rule, created and configured entirely in a committed script (`scripts/setup_shadow_programme.py`), never by hand. Concretely:

- `events.put_rule(Name="solace-shadow-tick", ScheduleExpression="rate(5 minutes)", State="DISABLED")`. Created DISABLED. Enabling is a deliberate, separate act (`--enable` flag), so provisioning the programme cannot accidentally start billing. This is the direct answer to `solace-warmer`, whose schedule and now-disabled state exist in no file in this repo (`grep -rn "solace-warmer"` returns only `scripts/deploy_container.py:26` and `scripts/enable_provisioned.py:21`, neither of which creates it).
- `events.put_targets(Rule="solace-shadow-tick", Targets=[{"Id":"shadow-lambda", "Arn":<shadow_arn>, "Input": json.dumps({"shadow_tick": True, "programme_id": PROGRAMME_ID}), "RetryPolicy": {"MaximumRetryAttempts": 0, "MaximumEventAgeInSeconds": 60}}])`.
- `lam.add_permission(FunctionName="solace-shadow", StatementId="eventbridge-shadow-tick", Principal="events.amazonaws.com", SourceArn=<rule arn>)`.

Target function, same image, different entrypoint:
- `lam.create_function(FunctionName="solace-shadow", PackageType="Image", Code={"ImageUri": <same digest as solace-api>}, ImageConfig={"Command": ["shadow.handler"]}, Role=<solace-shadow-exec>, Architectures=["arm64"], Timeout=120, MemorySize=2048, Environment={... SOLACE_MODE=aws, SHADOW_HOSPITAL_IDS, SHADOW_PROGRAMME_START/END ...})`. Verified this works: `Dockerfile.lambda` ends `CMD ["main.handler"]`, so `ImageConfig.Command` overrides it cleanly. `Dockerfile.lambda` needs one added line — `COPY backend/shadow.py ${LAMBDA_TASK_ROOT}/` — because it currently copies `backend/main.py` by name, not the directory.
- `lam.put_function_concurrency(FunctionName="solace-shadow", ReservedConcurrentExecutions=1)`.
- `lam.put_function_event_invoke_config(FunctionName="solace-shadow", MaximumRetryAttempts=0, MaximumEventAgeInSeconds=60)`.

The script is idempotent and re-asserts all four settings on every run, so a redeploy cannot silently drop them.

WHY NOT the existing `solace-api` Lambda. It is technically possible and I checked it carefully: `backend/main.py:266` is `if isinstance(event, dict) and (event.get("warmup") or event.get("source") == "aws.events")`. A constant-`Input` target produces an event with NEITHER key, so it falls through to `_mangum(event, context)` at line 283, where no Mangum inferer matches and it raises RuntimeError — an async invocation failure, precisely the retry-amplified error class from 42abe22. A raw (non-constant-Input) EventBridge delivery carries `source == "aws.events"` and gets swallowed into the warmup branch: a dry predict on the fake patient at `main.py:236-241`, a 200 response, `{"warm": true}`, and nobody scored. That failure reports SUCCESS in CloudWatch, which for a programme whose only output is a ledger is the worst possible outcome. A third branch checked before line 266 on `event.get("shadow_tick")` avoids both and does not violate PERF-002 (CONSTITUTION.md:748-757 requires the warmup branch to exist and behave; it still does, and `{"warmup":true}` and `{"source":"aws.events"}` both still reach it). I rejected it only over reserved concurrency and IAM separation, as above.

WHY NOT EventBridge Scheduler. Its `EndDate` would auto-terminate the 90-day window, which is genuinely attractive. It costs a new IAM invocation role and a service `scripts/deploy_container.py` does not already speak. I put the window in code instead (`shadow.handler` refuses outside `[SHADOW_PROGRAMME_START, SHADOW_PROGRAMME_END]`), because the actual lesson of 42abe22 is that a control living only in AWS is unauditable — a hard kill in `shadow.py` is testable in the repo, a Scheduler EndDate is not.

WHY NOT Step Functions / per-patient fan-out. At BSW McKinney scale (HANDOFF.md:783, 43,301 visits/year ~ 119/day, ~4h LOS, census ~20-30, peak ~50) per-tick looping is 288 invocations/day and pays the catboost/shap/artifacts.pkl unpickle at most once per warm container. Per-patient fan-out is 6,000-14,000 invocations/day, each risking the cold start that measured 642 MB and 60+ s in 42abe22. Identical output, roughly 10x the cost, and it cannot batch its ledger writes anyway because `dynamodb:BatchWriteItem` is IAM-Denied (`scripts/iam_ledger_append_only.json`). If the census ever outgrows one bounded invocation, add a shard key to the rule rather than fanning out.
designs.enumeration_strategy:
Two Queries per hospital per tick, both with explicit KeyConditionExpressions, both paginated, zero `.scan()` anywhere. All boto3 lives in `backend/db/shadow_roster.py` per ARCH-002 (CONSTITUTION.md:328-335, L1).

STEP 1 — ENROL (find patients who arrived since the last tick).
`Query(TableName="solace-patients", IndexName="hospital_id-created_at-index", KeyConditionExpression="hospital_id = :h AND created_at > :since")`, looping on `LastEvaluatedKey`. `created_at` is the GSI RANGE key (`scripts/setup_aws.py:83-92`), so this is a sort-key seek, not a filter — it reads only rows created in the last ~5 minutes, typically 0-2 items. `:since` is a cursor stored as a roster item (`sk = "cursor#enrolment"`, attribute `last_created_at`), advanced to `max(created_at)` actually seen, never to `now`, so nothing is skipped. If a tick dies mid-way the cursor does not advance and the next tick re-reads the same window; enrolment is a conditional `PutItem` with `attribute_not_exists(sk)`, so re-reading is harmless.

This deliberately replaces the alternative of hooking `routers/intake.py:302`. It keeps the shadow programme entirely out of the intake hot path and out of the clinician request cycle. The cost is up to 5 minutes of enrolment latency, which is recorded (`enrolled_at` vs `arrival_at` on the roster item) and is a ledger-visible fact rather than a hidden one.

Each new encounter gets a roster item: `{hospital_id, sk: "open#<encounter_id>", encounter_id, programme_id, arrival_at (= patient created_at), enrolled_at, inputs_snapshot (JSON of transcript / medical_info / language — the fields nothing ever mutates after intake), last_vitals, last_input_fingerprint, last_scored_tick, last_full_score_tick, ttl (= PROGRAMME_END + retention, NOT 24h)}`.

STEP 2 — ENUMERATE (who is open right now).
`Query(TableName="solace-shadow-roster", KeyConditionExpression="hospital_id = :h AND begins_with(sk, :open)")` with `:open = "open#"`, looping on `LastEvaluatedKey`. `begins_with` on a sort key is a key condition, so DynamoDB seeks and reads only open encounters. After 90 days the partition holds ~10,800 items but this Query still reads only the ~25 open ones. Closing an encounter writes a `closed#<encounter_id>` item and deletes the `open#` one; if the delete fails the next tick sees a stale open item, finds nothing to score, and retries the close — self-healing.

WHY NOT the existing patient enumeration. `storage.list_patients_for_hospital` -> `_ddb_query_patients_by_hospital` (`backend/db/storage.py:181-187`) is a single unpaginated Query against an ALL-projection index, and `grep -rn 'LastEvaluatedKey\|ExclusiveStartKey' backend/` returns zero matches repo-wide. It silently truncates at DynamoDB's 1 MB page, and note that the 1 MB limit is applied BEFORE ProjectionExpression, so trimming the projection would not raise the item count. The patients rows are fat (~19 JSON blobs: transcript, prebrief, scribe, differential, workup, disposition, comfort_protocol, shap_values, ai_processing_log — `routers/intake.py:263-297`), so truncation arrives at a low census. Patients dropped by truncation would be indistinguishable from patients who left — exactly the population the under-triage rate is about.

PERF-004 (CONSTITUTION.md:771-780) is L2 and its written scope is only the three hot-path routers, so a scheduler is outside its letter. Its stated check — `.query()` with an explicit KeyConditionExpression — is satisfied by both queries above. The only DynamoDB `.scan(` in the repo remains `scripts/rotate_pins.py:51`, offline.

WEEK 14. Query the roster partition for the hospital (both `open#` and `closed#`), get every `encounter_id` in the programme, then `encounter_ledger.timeline(eid)` per encounter. The ledger allow (`scripts/iam_ledger_allow.json`) grants only PutItem/GetItem/Query and the table has no GSI, so the ledger can never enumerate itself — the roster is what makes the report computable, and it survives long after the patient row's 24h/30-minute TTL has fired.
designs.idempotency:
The tick identity is `tick_id = floor(unix_epoch_now / 300)` — derived from the wall clock, NOT from anything in the event payload. Two deliveries of the same schedule, a Lambda retry, and a manual re-invoke inside the same 5-minute window all compute the same `tick_id`. Every entry the shadow scorer writes — prediction, no-change event, refusal, gap, heartbeat — carries `output["tick_id"]`.

DUPLICATE TRIGGER. Before scoring encounter E: `tail = encounter_ledger.tail(E)` (a new one-item accessor, see below). If `tail is not None and tail.output.get("tick_id", -1) >= tick_id`, skip. This is authoritative because it reads the ledger, not a cache, and it costs nothing extra — `record()` already needs the tail to allocate a sequence number. The roster's `last_scored_tick` is a fast-path hint only; the ledger is the arbiter, so a crash between the ledger write and the roster update cannot produce a duplicate entry.

OVERLAPPING RUNS. `ReservedConcurrentExecutions=1` plus `MaximumRetryAttempts=0` means an invoke arriving while a tick is still running is throttled and dropped rather than queued. Function `Timeout=120` is under the 300 s cadence, so this should never happen; when it does, the dropped tick is recorded retrospectively as a cadence gap by the next tick. Even without the concurrency cap, two overlapping runs carry different `tick_id`s and the tail check makes the overlap harmless.

LAMBDA RETRIES. `put_function_event_invoke_config(MaximumRetryAttempts=0, MaximumEventAgeInSeconds=60)` on the function AND `RetryPolicy` on the EventBridge target. Both layers, because they are different mechanisms (EventBridge retrying the async invoke API call vs. Lambda's own internal async retry). Even if one leaked, the `tick_id` check makes a retry a no-op.

COLD STARTS. Nothing survives in container memory by design. The roster lives in DynamoDB; sequence numbers come from a strongly-consistent tail read of the ledger; the cursor is a roster item. A brand-new container produces byte-identical behaviour to a warm one. This matters because `triage_ml.predict()` is fully deterministic — `build_row` hard-codes `arrival_hour=12`, `arrival_day="Monday"`, `arrival_season="winter"`, `shift="day"`, `site_id="demo"` (`backend/services/triage_ml.py:326-334`), so wall-clock time never enters the feature vector and identical inputs cannot yield a different score.

PARTIAL DATA. `input_fingerprint = sha256(canonical_json({inputs_snapshot, vitals}))`. Three outcomes:
- fingerprint changed -> full prediction entry.
- fingerprint unchanged and `tick_id - last_full_score_tick < 12` -> `model="event"` entry `{"kind": "rescore_no_input_change", "tick_id": ..., "fingerprint": ..., "unchanged_since_tick": ...}`. Honest, because the score provably cannot have changed, and it keeps the cadence auditable without writing 288 identical predictions per patient per day.
- fingerprint unchanged but 12 ticks (1 hour) have passed -> full prediction anyway, so an auditor sees a real score with a real conformal set at least hourly regardless.

COMPLETENESS REFUSAL. Counted outside `predict()`, because `predict()` cannot report it: `build_row` silently substitutes clinically normal values for every absent vital (`gcs_total or 15` at :346, `mental_status or "alert"` at :323, `shock_index 0.8` at :351, weight/height/bmi 70/170/24 at :348-350, training-set medians at :366-368), and the `miss_*` indicator features are dead at inference because imputation runs before they are computed (:366-370 vs `scripts/train_triage_model.py:171-179`). If fewer than `SHADOW_MIN_VITALS_PRESENT` (default 3) of {systolic_bp, diastolic_bp, heart_rate, respiratory_rate, temperature_c, spo2} are real, the scorer writes `model="event"` `{"kind": "score_refused_incomplete", "present": [...], "missing": [...]}` and emits NO prediction. Without this the ledger fills with "ESI 3, vitals normal" computed entirely from imputed defaults, and the week-14 under-triage number is garbage.

LEDGER-SIDE FIXES REQUIRED BEFORE ANY OF THIS RUNS (all in `backend/services/encounter_ledger.py`, storage moved to `backend/db/ledger_store.py`):
- Tail-only numbering. `record()` needs only `len(chain)` and `chain[-1].entry_hash`. Replace the full-chain read with `tail(eid)` = `Query(..., ScanIndexForward=False, Limit=1, ConsistentRead=True)`, `seq = tail.seq + 1`. This removes the O(n) read per write AND removes the permanent-wedge bug at its source: today `_load_all` (`:182-187`) has no `LastEvaluatedKey` loop, so once a chain exceeds 1 MB the read truncates, `seq = len(chain)+1` comes back too low, the conditional PutItem fails, all 8 attempts at `_MAX_SEQ_ATTEMPTS` burn, and `record()` raises `LedgerUnavailable` forever on every container. At the heartbeat chain's 288 entries/day for 90 days (25,920 entries) that is not hypothetical.
- Paginate `_load_all` anyway, for `timeline()` and `verify()`, which genuinely need the whole chain. Without it `verify()` returns `ok=True` on a truncated prefix — an incomplete record claiming to be intact.
- Fix the fabrication bug at `:327`: `chain = _load_all(encounter_id) or chain + [entry]` inserts an entry that just FAILED to persist. The process then reports `verify()==ok` with 2 entries while 1 row reached the store, and after a cold start the same encounter reports `ok=False, broken_at=1, reason="sequence gap"` — the ledger accusing itself of tampering on a record nobody touched. Replace with: re-read the tail; if the conditional check failed, an item exists by definition, so an empty re-read is an error -> raise `LedgerUnavailable`. Never synthesize.
- Bound the cache. `_entries` (`:90`) is a process-global dict with no eviction outside the test-only `reset()`. Under tail-only numbering nothing needs the full chain, so replace with an `OrderedDict` of tails capped at 512 encounters; eviction costs one 1-item Query.
- Wrap the read path. `_chain()` is called at `:300`, OUTSIDE the try that begins at `:320`, so a `ClientError` from a throttled read escapes `record()` unwrapped and is not caught by either existing caller (`triage.py:113`, `clinical_ai.py:495`). The scorer catches broadly per encounter regardless, but this should be fixed so one throttled read cannot kill a whole tick.

failure_modes.mode: EventBridge event reaches a handler that answers it as a warm ping and reports success while scoring nobody
failure_modes.handling: The rule targets `solace-shadow`, a separate function whose `shadow.handler` has no warmup branch and no Mangum adapter. It reads `event["shadow_tick"]` and refuses (returns `{"ok": False, "reason": "unrecognised_event"}` and logs at error) on anything else. `backend/main.py:266` is untouched, so PERF-002 (CONSTITUTION.md:748-757) and the deploy smoke test at `scripts/deploy_container.py:174-184` are unaffected.
failure_modes.test: `test_shadow_scheduler_is_bounded.py::test_a_warmup_event_is_not_a_tick` — feed `shadow.handler` the exact payloads `{"warmup": true}`, `{"source": "aws.events", "detail-type": "Scheduled Event"}` and `{}`; assert none produce a scoring pass and none return `{"warm": true}`. Mirror: feed `main.handler` `{"shadow_tick": true}` and assert it does NOT reach the ledger.

failure_modes.mode: A tick hangs (cold `_load()` unpickling catboost/shap, a stalled DynamoDB call) and consumes the whole function timeout, which Lambda retries — the exact 42abe22 mechanism
failure_modes.handling: Three independent bounds. (1) Per-encounter: the score runs on a daemon thread joined with an 8 s timeout, the pattern from `backend/main.py:253-257`, chosen because 42abe22 records that a between-steps deadline check was written FIRST and was useless — the call that hung was `_load()` and it never returned to be checked. (2) Per-invocation: `SHADOW_TICK_BUDGET_SECONDS = 45`, clamped to `remaining_ms/1000 - 15`, checked before starting each encounter. (3) Structural: `Timeout=120`, `ReservedConcurrentExecutions=1`, `MaximumRetryAttempts=0`. Two per-encounter timeouts in one tick abort the tick — the container is sick. The runaway thread is not killed (Python cannot) but Lambda freezes the container on handler return, so billing follows the handler, not the thread.
failure_modes.test: `test_shadow_scheduler_is_bounded.py`, mirroring `backend/tests/test_warmup_is_bounded.py`: monkeypatch `triage_ml.predict` to `time.sleep(300)`, assert the tick returns in under 15 s; assert the response says it gave up rather than reporting success; assert `shadow._tick_budget(_Context(5_000)) < 5.0`; assert `SHADOW_TICK_BUDGET_SECONDS * 2 < FUNCTION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. Plus `test_shadow_deploy_config.py` asserting `scripts/setup_shadow_programme.py` contains `MaximumRetryAttempts=0`, `ReservedConcurrentExecutions=1` and `State="DISABLED"`.

failure_modes.mode: A ledger chain crosses DynamoDB's 1 MB Query page; the encounter is permanently wedged and `verify()` reports ok=True on the truncated prefix
failure_modes.handling: Tail-only numbering (`ScanIndexForward=False, Limit=1, ConsistentRead=True`) so `record()` never reads more than one item and chain length is irrelevant to writes; `load_all` paginated on `LastEvaluatedKey` for `timeline()`/`verify()`. Additionally the no-change-event policy caps a 24 h boarding stay at ~24 full prediction entries plus ~264 small events instead of 288 SHAP-bearing entries, which keeps chains an order of magnitude smaller.
failure_modes.test: `test_encounter_ledger_durability.py`: with a fake table holding 400 entries whose combined size exceeds one simulated page, assert `record()` allocates seq=401 (not a repeat), assert `timeline()` returns all 400, and assert `verify()` returns `checked == 400`. Regression test: with `load_all` artificially truncated, assert `verify()` reports failure rather than `ok=True`.

failure_modes.mode: A bare ESI number reaches the ledger with no conformal set or SHAP attribution
failure_modes.handling: Harden the write path itself, not the caller. `_check_uncertainty` (`encounter_ledger.py:253-265`) currently only checks that the literal key `"coverage"` is present — I verified `{"coverage": None}` is accepted. Extend it into `_check_prediction`: for any `model != "event"`, require `uncertainty["coverage"]` to be a float in (0, 1], `uncertainty["conformal_set"]` to be a non-empty list, `uncertainty["coverage_source"]` to be a non-empty string, and `output["top_features"]` to be a non-empty list. Verified the existing caller at `routers/triage.py:103-112` already satisfies all four, so this is not a breaking change. Requirement 2 becomes structural for every caller, present and future.
failure_modes.test: `test_encounter_ledger.py::test_a_bare_number_cannot_be_recorded` — parametrize over `uncertainty=None`, `{}`, `{"coverage": None}`, `{"coverage": 0.9}` (no conformal_set), and an output with `top_features=[]`; assert `MissingUncertainty` on every one. Plus `test_the_event_exemption_is_an_exact_string`: `model="Event"` and `model="gap"` are rejected, `model="event"` is not.

failure_modes.mode: A shadow score reaches a clinician screen or an EHR write-back
failure_modes.handling: Four layers. (1) IAM: `solace-shadow-exec` has an explicit `Deny` on `dynamodb:PutItem`/`UpdateItem`/`DeleteItem` for `table/solace-patients`, and no permission on `solace-notes`, SNS, SES or the EHR tables. A Deny beats every Allow. (2) Import closure: the shadow package never imports `services.workflows`, `lib.claude`, `services.transcription`, `services.tts`, `services.voice_agent.*`, `services.hl7_v2`, `services.fhir_writer`, `services.sms`, `services.email`, `httpx` or `requests`. Critically it does NOT copy `routers/triage.py:68-78` (which writes `refined_esi_level`, displayed in preference to `esi_level` by `frontend/src/components/clinician/PatientCard.tsx:20-22`) or `routers/triage.py:121-136` (`_wf.fire`, one call reaching send_sms / send_slack_webhook / http_webhook / create_clinician_note / set_patient_field / ehr_write / notify at `services/workflows/actions.py:375-520`). (3) No route: the shadow function has no API Gateway integration and `main.py` includes no shadow router. (4) Read-side: `routers/encounters.py:56` and `:83` currently return every ledger entry to any authenticated clinician, so shadow entries would be visible on request — filter `model.startswith("shadow_")` out of both responses for the duration of the programme.
failure_modes.test: `test_shadow_has_no_egress.py` (rule SHADOW-001, L1), built on the SEC-004 machinery in `backend/tests/services/test_consent_gate.py:118-164`: compute the forward import closure from `{shadow, services.shadow_scorer, db.shadow_roster}` and assert it intersects the egress-leaf set in exactly zero places, with an `ALLOWED_EGRESS: dict[str,str]` whose correct steady state is EMPTY plus a staleness test. AST-assert the set of qualified calls in the shadow package is a subset of an explicit allowlist. AST-assert no FunctionDef in the package carries a `get/post/put/patch/delete` decorator. Then DRIVE it, because both existing derived-scope tests do and CONSTITUTION.md:24-27 says a cited line proves nothing: in local mode, seed one patient, install spies on `storage.update_patient`, `storage.put_patient`, `storage.add_note`, `workflows.engine.fire`, `sms.send`, `email.send_email`, `httpx.Client.post` and `lib.claude.messages_create`, run one tick, assert every spy has zero calls and `encounter_ledger.timeline(pid)` gained exactly one entry with `verify(pid).ok is True`.

failure_modes.mode: A tick does not run at all (rule disabled, invoke throttled, event dropped, region issue) — a silent cadence gap
failure_modes.handling: Two detectors. Retrospective, per encounter: the next tick compares `tick_id` against the tail's `tick_id` and, if the difference exceeds 1, writes one `model="event"` entry `{"kind": "cadence_gap", "from_tick": ..., "to_tick": ..., "missed_ticks": N}` on that encounter's chain. This is the honest construction — a gap can only ever be recorded by a later observer, never by the process that did not run. Programme-level: a heartbeat chain at reserved encounter_id `shadow-heartbeat#<hospital_id>#<programme_id>` gets one `model="event"` entry per tick carrying `{tick_id, census, scored, refused, no_change, missed, budget_exhausted}`, so week 14 can reconstruct exactly which of the ~25,900 scheduled ticks ran without reading a single patient chain. Live: a CloudWatch alarm on `solace-shadow` Invocations < 250 over 24 h.
failure_modes.test: `test_shadow_scorer.py::test_a_skipped_tick_becomes_a_ledger_event` — score at tick N, then invoke at tick N+3, assert the chain gained a `cadence_gap` entry with `missed_ticks == 2` before the new score. `::test_the_heartbeat_records_every_tick` — run three ticks, assert three heartbeat entries with consecutive tick_ids and `verify()` ok.

failure_modes.mode: The patient row is TTL-deleted mid-stay, so the scorer loses the inputs it needs
failure_modes.handling: Real and unavoidable today: `db/storage.py:29` sets a 24 h TTL, `routers/patients.py:190` drops it to 30 MINUTES once a clinician marks the patient seen, and `routers/patients.py:197-199` documents that DynamoDB sweeps up to ~48 h late. 'Seen' is a first-contact marker, not a departure marker — `db/constants.py` has only `waiting` and `seen`, and there is no discharge event in the schema at all. The roster item's `inputs_snapshot` (transcript, medical_info, language — fields nothing ever mutates after intake) plus `last_vitals` make the roster self-sufficient: scoring continues from the roster when the patient row is gone. `db.shadow_roster.get_patient_or_snapshot(eid)` returns the live row when present and the snapshot when not, and the ledger entry records which (`inputs["source"] = "live_row" | "roster_snapshot"`). This is a mitigation, not a fix — the 30-minute TTL should still be reconciled with the programme before week 1, and because raising it widens the PHI retention footprint that `routers/patients.py:177-183` documents as a deliberate HIPAA-minimisation control, that is a compliance decision for counsel, not a config tweak.
failure_modes.test: `test_shadow_scorer.py::test_scoring_survives_a_deleted_patient_row` — enrol an encounter, run one tick, delete the patient row, run a second tick; assert a prediction entry is still written and `inputs["source"] == "roster_snapshot"`.

failure_modes.mode: An encounter is never closed and is re-scored forever, inflating the week-14 denominator
failure_modes.handling: There is NO departure signal in the schema, so this is a heuristic and the design says so out loud. Close when either: (a) the patient row is absent AND the fingerprint has been unchanged for `SHADOW_STALE_TICKS` (default 24 = 2 hours), or (b) `now - arrival_at > SHADOW_MAX_LOS_HOURS` (default 24). Every close writes a `model="event"` entry `{"kind": "encounter_closed", "reason": "stale_no_row" | "max_los" | "explicit"}`, so the week-14 analysis can partition its cohort by how each encounter ended and discount timeout-closed ones. A real discharge signal (an ADT feed, or a `discharged_at` attribute set by a new clinician action) should replace the heuristic and would slot in as `reason="explicit"` with no other change.
failure_modes.test: `test_shadow_scorer.py::test_a_stale_encounter_closes_and_says_why` — enrol, delete the patient row, advance the clock past the stale window, assert the roster item moved from `open#` to `closed#` and a `encounter_closed` event with `reason="stale_no_row"` is the last chain entry. `::test_max_los_closes_a_live_encounter` for branch (b).

failure_modes.mode: One encounter's failure (throttled read, malformed row, LedgerUnavailable) aborts the whole tick and the rest of the department is never scored
failure_modes.handling: The per-encounter body is wrapped in a broad `except Exception`. On failure the scorer records `model="event"` `{"kind": "score_failed", "error_class": type(e).__name__, "tick_id": ...}` on that encounter's chain (best-effort; if THAT write also fails, increment a module counter reported in the tick summary and logged) and continues to the next encounter. This matters because the ledger read path currently escapes unwrapped — `_chain()` is called at `encounter_ledger.py:300`, outside the try beginning at `:320`, so a `ClientError` propagates raw and neither existing caller (`triage.py:113`, `clinical_ai.py:495`) would catch it. `shadow.handler` NEVER raises; it always returns a summary dict, so an async invocation failure (the retry-amplified class from 42abe22) is structurally impossible even with retries misconfigured.
failure_modes.test: `test_shadow_scorer.py::test_one_bad_encounter_does_not_stop_the_tick` — three enrolled encounters, `predict` raises for the middle one; assert the outer two get prediction entries, the middle gets a `score_failed` event, and the tick summary reports `failed == 1`. `::test_the_handler_never_raises` — make `db.shadow_roster.list_open` raise `ClientError`; assert `handler()` returns a dict with `ok is False` rather than propagating.

failure_modes.mode: The safety floor silently lowers acuity, or is absent from the path that writes to the ledger
failure_modes.handling: Today the floor is applied three different ways and only one is correct: raise-only with a strict `<` at `services/triage.py:133-140`; UNCONDITIONALLY at `routers/intake.py:192-196` (`if shortcut: esi_level = shortcut.esi_level`, so an ESI-5 administrative match can overwrite a higher-acuity engine output); and completely ABSENT from `routers/triage.py`, which is the only path that currently writes to the ledger — `routers/triage.py:20` imports `encounter_ledger, triage_ml` and never imports `triage_rules`. Lift the raise-only form into one shared `backend/services/triage_floor.apply_floor()` and have both `services/triage.py` and the shadow scorer call it. The ledger entry records both sides honestly: `output["model"]` = the raw ensemble result, `output["emitted"]` = the post-floor result, and when the floor fires `uncertainty["coverage_source"] = "safety_floor_override"` with `uncertainty["floor_rule"] = shortcut.reason`, because the model's conformal coverage no longer describes the emitted singleton set.
failure_modes.test: `test_triage_floor.py::test_the_floor_can_only_raise_acuity` — a property test over the full 5x5 cross product of (engine ESI, rule ESI) asserting `apply_floor(...).esi_level <= engine_esi` always, and `== engine_esi` whenever `rule_esi >= engine_esi`. Plus `test_shadow_scorer.py::test_every_shadow_score_passes_through_the_floor` — a transcript containing 'not breathing' with an engine output of ESI 3 must produce an emitted ESI of 1 and `source` beginning `safety_floor+`.

failure_modes.mode: Audit rows written by the tick are lost when the handler returns
failure_modes.handling: `lib/audit.py:156-160` dispatches to the default asyncio executor and returns; Lambda freezes the container the instant the handler returns, so queued rows die silently. `shadow.handler` is a plain synchronous function (not `async def`), so `asyncio.get_running_loop()` raises `RuntimeError` and audit takes the `_write_sync(item)` fallback — synchronous by construction. One audit row per tick, not per patient: `action="shadow.tick"` (deliberately NOT starting with `abuse.`, which would feed the blocklist at `lib/audit.py:170-184`), `clinician_id=None`, `clinician_name="Shadow Programme"`, `extra={tick_id, hospital_id, census, scored, refused, missed}`. Per-patient evidence lives in the ledger, which is stronger than the audit log. COMP-002's written scope is `backend/routers/*.py`, so it does not literally reach a scheduler — this is the obligation re-derived rather than skipped.
failure_modes.test: `test_shadow_has_no_egress.py::test_the_handler_is_not_async` — `assert not inspect.iscoroutinefunction(shadow.handler)`, with the reason in the assertion message. `test_shadow_scorer.py::test_the_tick_is_audited_once` — spy on `audit.record`, run a tick over three encounters, assert exactly one call with `action == "shadow.tick"` and `not action.startswith("abuse.")`.

failure_modes.mode: The scheduler runs outside AWS mode and records the entire 90-day programme into a dict that dies with the process
failure_modes.handling: `encounter_ledger._persist` returns at line 143-144 before touching DynamoDB when `settings.solace_mode != "aws"`, and `_load_all` returns `[]` at :177-178 — so a misconfigured scheduler would report success while writing nowhere. `config.assert_deployment_is_configured` (`lib/config.py:128-135`) protects Lambda but nothing else. `shadow.handler` refuses at the top: if `settings.solace_mode != "aws"` it logs at error and returns `{"ok": False, "reason": "refusing_to_run_outside_aws_mode"}` without scoring anything, following the `harden_for_deployment` precedent at `lib/config.py:148-166` that 'a comment saying MUST is not a control'. Also refuses outside `[SHADOW_PROGRAMME_START, SHADOW_PROGRAMME_END]`, so the programme cannot outlive its own 90-day window even if the rule is left enabled.
failure_modes.test: `test_shadow_scheduler_is_bounded.py::test_it_refuses_to_run_in_local_mode` — set `solace_mode="local"`, assert the tick scores nothing and says why. `::test_it_refuses_outside_the_programme_window` — freeze the clock one day past `SHADOW_PROGRAMME_END`, assert `reason == "outside_programme_window"` and zero ledger writes.

failure_modes.mode: The next `deploy_container.py` run silently restores the 42abe22 retry amplification on solace-api
failure_modes.handling: Not caused by this design but adjacent to it and worth fixing in the same change, because the shadow programme inherits the account's habits. `git show 42abe22 --stat` touches only `Dockerfile.lambda`, `backend/main.py` and `backend/tests/test_warmup_is_bounded.py` — the two config fixes (disable the rule, retries=0 with 60 s max event age) exist only in the console. `grep -rn 'MaximumRetryAttempts|put_function_event_invoke_config|MaximumEventAge'` returns zero hits repo-wide. `scripts/deploy_container.py:89` deletes the function on the Zip->Image path, discarding any EventInvokeConfig, and `:157-161` calls `put_targets` with the same target Id and no `RetryPolicy`, actively erasing any target-level policy set by hand. Add `lam.put_function_event_invoke_config(FunctionName="solace-api", MaximumRetryAttempts=0, MaximumEventAgeInSeconds=60)` and a `RetryPolicy` on the warmer target, both in the script.
failure_modes.test: `test_shadow_deploy_config.py::test_the_deploy_script_pins_async_retries` — read `scripts/deploy_container.py` as text and assert it contains `put_function_event_invoke_config`, `MaximumRetryAttempts=0` and a `RetryPolicy` on the warmer target, with the assertion message naming commit 42abe22. Same shape as `test_dev_echo_is_never_deployed.py:96-102` ('a guard nothing calls is decoration').

designs.cost_estimate:
SIZING. HANDOFF.md:783 gives BSW McKinney at 43,301 ED visits/year ~ 119/day. At a 4-6 h LOS the average census is ~20-30 and the peak maybe 50. Cadence `rate(5 minutes)` = 288 invocations/day = 8,640/month.

LAMBDA. Per warm tick: 1 roster Query + 1 patients-GSI Query + ~20-25 `triage_ml.predict()` calls + ~20-25 ledger tail reads + ~20-25 conditional PutItems + 1 heartbeat write. Per-predict latency is UNMEASURED (see unknowns — no artifacts on this filesystem, no benchmark in the repo); I budget 50 ms warm on a 2048 MB arm64 container, giving ~1.3 s of compute plus ~0.6 s of DynamoDB round-trips ~ 2 s per tick. A 5-minute cadence keeps at least one container warm essentially all the time, so cold starts should be a handful per day; I budget 10/day at +15 s each.

  288 x 2 s x 2 GB           = 1,152 GB-s/day  -> 34,560 GB-s/month -> ~$0.46
  10 cold starts x 15 s x 2 GB = 300 GB-s/day  ->  9,000 GB-s/month -> ~$0.12
  8,640 requests x $0.20/M                                          -> ~$0.002
  Lambda total                                                      -> ~$0.60/month

DYNAMODB (on-demand). Writes ~ 288 x 22 = 6,336/day = 190k/month. Ledger items with SHAP `top_features` run ~2-3 KB, so ~570k WRU at $1.25/M -> ~$0.71. Reads: ~6,300 strongly-consistent 1-item tail Queries/day plus 576 partition Queries -> ~190k RRU/month -> ~$0.05. Roster writes ~190k small items -> ~$0.24. DynamoDB total ~ $1.00/month. Note the no-change-event policy is doing real work here: without it, full SHAP-bearing entries every 5 minutes would roughly quadruple the write bytes.

CLOUDWATCH. ~288 short log streams/day, a few MB/month, plus 6 alarms at $0.10 -> ~$1/month.

NEW TABLE. `solace-shadow-roster` is PAY_PER_REQUEST with PITR; storage over 90 days is ~10,800 items x ~5 KB = ~55 MB -> under $0.02/month.

TOTAL: roughly $2-3/month for the whole shadow programme. Under $10/month even if my per-predict estimate is 4x optimistic.

WHY THIS CANNOT REPEAT 42abe22. That incident cost $14.56 of Lambda in a 30-day window (out of $28.76 total AWS spend) because a scheduled invocation with NO time budget ran to the 60 s timeout, a timeout is a failure, Lambda's default two async retries tripled it, and 360 pings/day became exactly 1,080 minute-long 2 GB invocations. It ran for weeks and was found by reading an invoice. Seven things are different here, and the first three make it structurally impossible rather than merely unlikely:

1. HARD CEILING. `ReservedConcurrentExecutions=1` on `solace-shadow` means at most one 2 GB execution exists at any instant. Combined with `Timeout=120` and 288 triggers/day, the absolute worst case — every single tick hanging to the full timeout for a whole month — is 288 x 120 s x 2 GB = 69,120 GB-s/day = 2.07M GB-s/month ~ $27.60. That is the ceiling the resource configuration enforces, independent of any code being correct. 42abe22 had no ceiling at all.
2. RETRIES ZERO, IN CODE, IN TWO PLACES. `put_function_event_invoke_config(MaximumRetryAttempts=0, MaximumEventAgeInSeconds=60)` on the function and `RetryPolicy={"MaximumRetryAttempts": 0, "MaximumEventAgeInSeconds": 60}` on the EventBridge target, both in `scripts/setup_shadow_programme.py`, both asserted by `test_shadow_deploy_config.py`. The 3x multiplier is the specific thing that turned a bug into a bill, and its mitigation currently exists ONLY in the live account.
3. THE HANDLER NEVER RAISES. It catches everything and returns a summary dict. An async invocation that returns 200 is not a retryable failure at all, so the amplification path has no input even if (1) and (2) were both misconfigured.
4. TIME BUDGET OF THE PROVEN SHAPE. 45 s in-handler budget on a 120 s function, enforced by a daemon thread joined with a timeout per encounter plus a deadline check between encounters. 42abe22 records that a between-steps check alone was written first and was useless because `_load()` never returned to be checked; both together is the complete fix.
5. THE RULE IS BORN DISABLED and the handler enforces `SHADOW_PROGRAMME_START/END` independently, so the programme self-terminates at day 90 even if nobody remembers to turn the rule off. `solace-warmer` ran unnoticed for weeks because nothing could stop it except a human noticing an invoice.
6. ALARMS THAT WOULD ACTUALLY HAVE FIRED. The existing `solace-lambda-errors` alarm triggers above 5 errors per 5-minute period (`scripts/setup_cloudwatch_alarms.py:48-54` with the `period=300, evaluations=1` defaults at :25); the incident ran at ~3.75 per window and sat under the threshold for weeks. The new set: `solace-shadow-errors` Sum > 0 (this handler should never error), `solace-shadow-duration` p99 > 72 s (60% of timeout), `solace-shadow-invocations-high` Sum > 15 per 5 min (a cadence that speeds up is the runaway signature), `solace-shadow-invocations-low` Sum < 250 per 24 h (the cadence stopped), `solace-shadow-throttles` Sum > 0. And separately, the ten existing DynamoDB alarms at `scripts/setup_cloudwatch_alarms.py:73-80` alarm on `UserErrors` dimensioned by `TableName`, but `UserErrors` is an account-and-region aggregate with no `TableName` dimension — with `TreatMissingData="notBreaching"` all ten sit permanently OK on no data. Fix the metric to `ThrottledRequests`/`WriteThrottleEvents` and add `solace-encounter-ledger` and `solace-shadow-roster`, neither of which is in the list today.
7. A BUDGET ALARM. An AWS Budgets monthly threshold at $50 with an SNS notification. `grep` for `EstimatedCharges` or Budgets across this repo returns nothing — the account has never had one, which is why the last incident was discovered manually.

One more structural protection: `scripts/deploy_container.py:85-90` deletes and recreates `solace-api` on the Zip->Image path, which wipes function-level config. `solace-shadow` is created and maintained by a different script that never deletes it and re-asserts concurrency, retry and event-invoke config idempotently on every run.
