Interleaving: at 14:20:03 tick N writes seq=41 (tick_id=N); at 14:20:07 a nurse submits refine-triage, writing seq=42 with no tick_id; at 14:20:11 a duplicate EventBridge delivery (at-least-once is documented, not theoretical) re-runs tick N; tail is seq=42, `.get("tick_id", -1)` returns -1, `-1 >= N` is False, so the patient is scored and recorded AGAIN at seq=43 with tick_id=N. Two prediction entries for one tick, both cryptographically valid, denominator inflated. The same defect corrupts gap detection in the opposite direction: `tail_tick_id < tick_id - 1` evaluates `-1 < N-1`, which is true, so every tick that follows any clinician entry writes a bogus cadence_gap claiming `missed_ticks` ≈ tick_id (a number in the tens of thousands by day 90) onto the chain the recognition-delay report is computed from. The correct read is 'last SHADOW-authored entry', which `latest(encounter_id, model=...)` at encounter_ledger.py:349-357 already provides — but it walks the whole chain via `_chain()`, i.e. exactly the O(n) read the tail-only rewrite exists to eliminate. The design's own fix and its own idempotency scheme are mutually exclusive and it does not see the collision.

`record()` IS NOT INTERNALLY IDEMPOTENT, SO A LOST RESPONSE PRODUCES A DUPLICATE SCORE THE tick_id CHECK CANNOT SEE. The conditional put is `attribute_not_exists(encounter_id) AND attribute_not_exists(seq)` (encounter_ledger.py:165-171) and botocore retries DynamoDB calls automatically. Sequence: PutItem for seq=41 is committed by DynamoDB; the HTTP response is lost to a socket timeout; botocore retries the byte-identical request; DynamoDB answers ConditionalCheckFailedException; `_persist` raises SequenceTaken; the retry loop at :322-328 re-reads the tail, finds seq=41 (its own entry), and writes an entry with identical inputs/output/tick_id at seq=42. Two identical predictions, same tick, chain verifies clean, and no downstream check can distinguish them from two genuine scores. This survives the design's tail-only rewrite untouched, because the duplicate is generated INSIDE record(), below the tick_id gate. It needs a content-idempotency check (compare the candidate's digest payload minus seq/prev_hash against the tail before writing) and the design has none.

THE 'MISSED CADENCE IS A LEDGER EVENT' CLAIM HAS A HOLE THAT IS INVISIBLE AND UNRECOVERABLE. The retrospective gap detector only writes a cadence_gap on chains that already have a roster item AND are re-scored later, and the heartbeat records missing TICKS, not missing PATIENTS. A 6-hour outage (rule disabled by a console mis-click, IAM change, reserved-concurrency throttle storm, region event) at 119 visits/day means roughly 30 patients arrive and are discharged entirely within the gap. They were never enrolled, so there is no roster item, no chain, no cadence_gap, no encounter_closed — zero trace. The only reconstruction path is the patients table, and backend/db/storage.py:29 TTLs it at 24h while backend/routers/patients.py:190 drops it to 30 MINUTES once a clinician marks the patient seen, with the sweep landing up to ~48h late (patients.py:197-199). So the evidence needed to even count what was missed is destroyed before anyone reads the heartbeat chain. Week 14 can say 'we missed 72 ticks' and cannot say 'we missed 30 patients', and the under-triage denominator shrinks silently in the flattering direction. Worse, the terminal case: if the programme dies on day 60 and never restarts, no later observer exists to record anything, and the sole detector is a CloudWatch alarm (Invocations < 250/24h) publishing to an SNS topic whose email subscription the codebase cannot confirm was ever accepted — a control living only in the AWS console, which is the exact anti-pattern this design correctly indicts solace-warmer for. The honest fix is an out-of-band arrival counter written at enrolment time and a dead-man's-switch that is itself in the ledger, not a graph.

THE DEPLOYED SHADOW CODE DRIFTS FROM THE TESTED CODE FOR 90 DAYS. `solace-shadow` is created once from 'the current solace-api image digest', and buildspec.yml's post_build runs `aws lambda update-function-code --function-name solace-api` and nothing else. Nothing in files_to_change touches buildspec.yml. Every subsequent CI deploy updates solace-api and leaves solace-shadow pinned to whatever digest existed at setup time — including, plausibly, an image predating the tail-only sequencing fix, the fabrication-bug fix at encounter_ledger.py:327, and the pagination fix. CI runs the full suite green against code the shadow function is not running. For a programme whose entire product is evidentiary, the ledger will record `model_version` for the ML artifacts and nothing at all about which scorer build produced the entry.

HARDENING `_check_uncertainty` INTO `_check_prediction` CAN 500 A LIVE CLINICIAN ENDPOINT AFTER A PARTIAL WRITE. `MissingUncertainty` subclasses ValueError (encounter_ledger.py:63) and routers/triage.py:114 catches ONLY `LedgerUnavailable`. The design adds four new rejection conditions (coverage a float in (0,1], non-empty conformal_set, non-empty coverage_source, non-empty output['top_features']) to the shared write path and asserts 'Verified the existing caller already satisfies all four, so this is not a breaking change' — but it verified the call-site SHAPE, not the runtime values. `top_features` comes from `_shap_top_features` (triage_ml.py:651+), which reshapes raw LightGBM pred_contrib output; any artifact whose feature_names disagree with the booster, or a future k<=0, yields []. When it does, refine_triage raises out of the try, AFTER `storage.update_patient` at line 78 has already written refined_esi_level to the patient row and BEFORE `_wf.fire` at line 121 — a 500 to the clinician, a refined score on the ED board, and no workflow. Any tightening of this shared gate needs the caller's except clause widened in the same change, and the design does not list routers/triage.py as modified.

THE CENSUS IS A SELF-SELECTED SUBSET, SO THE WEEK-14 NUMBER DOES NOT MEASURE THE DEPARTMENT. Enrolment reads solace-patients, and `storage.put_patient` has exactly ONE caller in the entire application: routers/intake.py:302. Every row in that table is a patient who completed Solace's own self-serve intake form. 'Re-score EVERY patient currently in the department' is therefore unachievable by construction — walk-ins who never touched the kiosk, EMS arrivals, and anyone triaged straight to a bed are invisible, and they are disproportionately the high-acuity patients an under-triage study is about. The design's weakest_point section names the vitals-staleness problem honestly but never states that the denominator itself is wrong; it treats the census as complete and spends its uncertainty budget on closure heuristics instead. This is the difference between 'the cadence may be uninformative' and 'the study measures a different population than it claims'.

TWO GOVERNANCE OBLIGATIONS ARE SKIPPED SILENTLY RATHER THAN DECIDED. (a) Consent: services/shadow_scorer.py's stated import list is triage_ml, triage_floor, encounter_ledger, db.shadow_roster, db.storage, lib.audit, lib.tenancy — `lib.consent` is absent, and no file, test or doc records the decision. Staying outside SEC-004's derived closure means the RULE does not fire; it does not mean 90 days of automated scoring on identified patients needs no legal basis. `lib/consent.py:89-98` exists specifically for background paths with no patient present. The right output is an explicit written 'treatment and operations, no gate' with counsel's name on it, mirroring how CONSTITUTION.md:108-111 handles the structurally identical voice question — not silence. (b) IAM: scripts/iam_shadow_exec_policy.json as specified grants DynamoDB, S3-less audit and KMS, and NO `logs:CreateLogGroup` / `CreateLogStream` / `PutLogEvents`. If that is the only policy attached to solace-shadow-exec, the function emits no CloudWatch logs at all, which silently guts the observability half of the 42abe22 story and makes the per-encounter score_failed diagnostics unreadable. The policy also grants no s3:PutObject for lib/audit.py's CMK-encrypted archive half of COMP-002.
winner.verdict: Strong on the money question, weak on the evidence question — and the evidence is the entire product. The 42abe22 defence is the best part and it is genuinely good: a separate function, ReservedConcurrentExecutions=1, retries pinned to 0 in code in two places, a handler that structurally never raises, the daemon-thread-join budget rather than a between-steps deadline, a rule born DISABLED, the programme window enforced in Python rather than in a console, a real budget alarm, and the correct catch that the ten existing DynamoDB alarms are dimensioned on a metric (UserErrors) that has no TableName dimension. The worst-case ceiling arithmetic (288 x 120s x 2GB ~ $27.60/mo) is honest and the pre-flight items (describe-table on the ledger, simulate-principal-policy for PutItem, measure one warm predict) are exactly right. Enumeration is mechanically valid against the real schema: the GSI exists with created_at as RANGE, both Queries use explicit KeyConditionExpressions, both paginate, no scan, boto3 confined to db/. PERF-004, ARCH-002, ARCH-001, SEC-004 and PERF-002 all hold. But the design makes one architectural choice — writing shadow entries onto the clinical encounter's own hash chain, because encounter_id == patient_id — and that choice cascades into four separate failures it does not see: shadow entries reachable by any authenticated clinician, a filter that cannot suppress the model="event" entries (one of which prints which vitals are missing, a live clinical nudge), a filtered timeline whose seq numbers and prev_hash links no longer verify for exactly the studied cohort, and a tail-based idempotency key that a single nurse's refine-triage call turns into duplicate scores plus cadence_gap entries claiming tens of thousands of missed ticks. A separate `shadow#<patient_id>` namespace kills all four at once and costs nothing. Independently, the enrolment cursor is unsound: strict `>` against a one-second-granularity created_at over an eventually-consistent GSI with no lookback window permanently drops patients, and the design states the opposite as a guarantee. And the missed-cadence claim, examined hard, detects missing ticks but not missing patients — the arrivals lost to an outage leave no trace anywhere, because the only record of them is TTL-deleted within 24 hours (30 minutes once seen). Not buildable as written. Buildable after: a separate ledger namespace, a lookback cursor, model-filtered idempotency, a content-idempotency guard inside record(), buildspec wiring for the shadow function, a widened except in routers/triage.py, logs: permissions, and a written consent determination. The core skeleton — one dedicated function, one tick, one roster, IAM as the shadow boundary — is the right skeleton and worth keeping.

all_hard_constraints: The re-score scheduler MUST NOT be dispatched by an EventBridge rule that reaches backend/main.py's handler() unchanged. handler() intercepts `event.get("source") == "aws.events"` and returns the warmup response, so a scheduled event would be silently answered as a warm ping and never re-score. Either dispatch on a distinct key checked BEFORE the warmup branch, or use a separate Lambda function. PERF-002 (CONSTITUTION.md:748) pins the existing warmup behaviour, so the warmup branch cannot simply be deleted.

Any new scheduled/async invocation MUST have MaximumRetryAttempts=0 and a MaximumEventAge set IN CODE, not by hand in the console. The identical protection from commit 42abe22 exists only in the live account and appears nowhere in this repo; scripts/deploy_container.py:89 deletes the function on one path, which discards EventInvokeConfig. Without codifying it, a failing 5-minute re-score becomes 3x invocations again — the precise mechanism that produced the $14.56 Lambda bill.

The re-score work MUST carry its own time budget and give up rather than run to the 60s Lambda timeout (deploy_container.py:124). Follow the pattern in main.py `_run_warmup` — a daemon thread joined with a timeout — because a deadline checked between steps bounds the gaps, not the steps, and the failure that cost money was a single call that never returned.
MUST NOT add a .scan() on solace-patients. Even outside PERF-004's literal three-file scope, a scan at <=5 minute cadence for 90 days reads every row in the table ~26,000 times.

MUST NOT enumerate via the existing hospital_id-created_at-index without fixing pagination first. backend/db/storage.py:182-187 is a single unpaginated .query() against an ALL-projection index; it silently truncates at 1MB. A scheduler built on it would drop the tail of the department — and the patients it drops would be indistinguishable from patients who left, which is exactly the population the under-triage rate is about.

MUST NOT rely on row existence in solace-patients to mean 'still in the department'. TTL is 24h by default (storage.py:29) and 30 minutes once seen (patients.py:190), and DynamoDB sweeps up to ~48h late (patients.py:197-198). A 90-day shadow programme measuring recognition delay over full length of stay cannot use a store that deletes boarding patients mid-stay on a nondeterministic schedule.

The 30-minute post-resolve TTL MUST be reconciled before the programme starts. 'seen' is a first-contact marker, not a departure marker — there is no departure marker in the schema at all (db/constants.py has only waiting/seen). Either add a real discharge event and make TTL depend on it, or exempt shadow-programme hospitals from TTL shortening. Note that raising the TTL directly widens the PHI retention footprint that patients.py:177-183 documents as a deliberate HIPAA-minimisation control, so this is a compliance decision, not a config tweak.

A durable encounter_id -> hospital_id mapping MUST exist somewhere that outlives the patient row, or the week-14 report cannot be computed. The ledger item has no hospital_id (encounter_ledger.py:148-163), the ledger has no GSI (setup_aws.py:170-180), and the patient row that carries hospital_id is deleted by TTL. Today nothing durable connects an encounter to a department.

Adding a GSI to solace-encounter-ledger requires amending scripts/iam_ledger_allow.json to cover /index/*, which breaks backend/tests/test_ledger_iam_policy.py:110-116 (`assert arn == LEDGER_ARN`). That test is a deliberate guard, so this is an explicit decision to make and document, not an incidental edit.

Ledger writes MUST be one conditional PutItem per entry — BatchWriteItem is IAM-denied (iam_ledger_append_only.json) and could not carry the append-only ConditionExpression anyway. Budget N sequential writes per cycle, serialized further by the module-level lock held across the round-trip (encounter_ledger.py:299-321).

encounter_ledger._entries (line 90) MUST be bounded before a long-lived scheduler uses it. It is a process-global dict populated read-through by _chain() and never evicted; a container re-scoring every patient every 5 minutes for 90 days grows it without limit on a 2048MB function.

Every re-score entry MUST carry uncertainty with a `coverage` key or encounter_ledger.record raises MissingUncertainty (encounter_ledger.py:253-265). A re-scorer emitting a bare ESI level fails at the write path.

New DynamoDB access code MUST live in backend/db/ per ARCH-002 (CONSTITUTION.md:328), and routers must reach it through the service/db layers per ARCH-001 (CONSTITUTION.md:316). The existing boto3-in-services violations (encounter_ledger.py:125, workflows/storage.py:28, voice_agent/session.py:200) are precedent, not license.

If the re-score path calls lib.claude (rather than only the local triage_ml LightGBM model), it enters SEC-004's derived scope (CONSTITUTION.md:88-90) and needs a consent check — against a consent record that currently lives only on the TTL-deleted patient row (intake.py:292-293).

Any new table or GSI MUST be created with the solace CMK per COMP-003; every existing setup script resolves alias/solace and passes SSESpecification (setup_aws.py:56-62, setup_abuse_prevention.py:62-66).

The scheduler MUST NOT be invoked by an EventBridge rule pointing at the existing solace Lambda function. backend/main.py:262 swallows any event with `source == "aws.events"` into the warmup path and returns before the app runs — the re-score would silently never happen while CloudWatch showed 100% success. Either use a separate function, or change the discriminator in handler() to require `event.get("warmup")` explicitly (and update scripts/deploy_container.py's warm-ping payload to match).

The scheduler MUST run in an environment where settings.solace_mode == "aws". In local mode _persist returns at encounter_ledger.py:144 and the entire 90-day ledger lives in a dict that dies with the container. This is enforced for Lambda by config.py:128-135 (a deployed process in local mode refuses to boot), but NOT for anything running outside Lambda — a container, an ECS task, or a laptop would silently record to nowhere and report success.

_load_all() MUST be made to paginate before any long-stay encounter is scored. At the target cadence a boarding patient generates ~288 entries/day; with inputs+output+uncertainty JSON per row, a multi-day stay crosses DynamoDB's 1MB Query page limit. Proven consequence: the encounter is permanently wedged — every write burns all 8 seq attempts and raises LedgerUnavailable forever — and verify() reports ok=True on the truncated prefix, so the record silently stops growing while claiming to be intact. This is the single failure mode that most directly destroys the week-14 report.

The scheduler MUST NOT rely on record() raising LedgerUnavailable for every failure. Read-path errors escape raw: _chain() is called at encounter_ledger.py:300, outside the try that begins at :320, so a DynamoDB ClientError from _load_all propagates unwrapped. Both existing callers (triage.py:113, clinical_ai.py:495) catch only LedgerUnavailable and would crash. A scheduler loop that dies on one patient's throttled read stops re-scoring the entire department.

The scheduler MUST NOT assume a warm-container success means a durable write. The SequenceTaken fallback at encounter_ledger.py:327 (`chain = _load_all(...) or chain + [entry]`) inserts a never-persisted entry into the in-memory chain when the re-read comes back empty. Verified: the process reports 2 entries and verify()==ok while only 1 row reached the store, and after a cold start the same encounter reports ok=False, broken_at=1, reason='sequence gap'. The ledger accuses itself of tampering on a record nobody touched — the worst possible outcome for a tamper-evidence claim.

Every scheduled score MUST carry a real uncertainty dict with a non-None coverage value. The gate at encounter_ledger.py:253-265 checks only that the key "coverage" exists — `{"coverage": None}` is accepted (verified by execution). triage_ml.predict() currently guarantees a float via DEFAULT_CONFORMAL_COVERAGE (triage_ml.py:618-620), but a scheduler that builds its own uncertainty dict can defeat the rule the whole ledger rests on without tripping a single test.

The scheduler MUST NOT pass `model="event"` for a score. The uncertainty exemption is an exact string match at encounter_ledger.py:254 and is the only bypass of the calibration rule. Conversely it MUST use exactly "event" (not "Event", not "gap", not "missed_cadence") for the missed-cadence gap records the shadow programme needs, or those writes will be rejected with MissingUncertainty.

The scheduler MUST set observed_at to the time the underlying data was observed, not the time of the write. The report's central claim is measured in minutes from observation. triage.py:93 already passes `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` while its own comment at :85-87 says it should not — do not copy that call site. Note also that observed_at is inside the hash (encounter_ledger.py:240) while recorded_at is NOT, so recorded_at is not defensible evidence.

The re-scoring loop MUST NOT hold the ledger's global lock across N patients in one invocation. encounter_ledger.py:91/:299 serialize every write behind one threading.Lock held across a DynamoDB round trip. With a 60s Lambda timeout (deploy_container.py:125) and the 42abe22 lesson that a scheduled invocation with no time budget consumes the entire timeout, retries twice, and bills 3x — the design needs an explicit per-invocation deadline and a bounded patient batch, not a loop that runs until the department is done.

Storage MUST be moved behind db/ or the L1 constitution violation gets institutionalized. encounter_ledger.py:125-129 initializes boto3 inside backend/services/, which ARCH-002 (CONSTITUTION.md:328-337, L1) forbids for exactly this directory. Nothing currently tests it. A scheduler that adds a second boto3 call site in services/ makes this harder to unwind, not easier.

The scheduler MUST NOT read the ledger to find out who to score. There is no enumerate API, no GSI on solace-encounter-ledger (setup_aws.py:170-180), and the IAM allow grants no Scan (iam_ledger_allow.json:6-14). The active-encounter list has to come from the patients table, and PERF-004 forbids .scan() there.

Retention MUST NOT be delegated to the caller. The ledger table deliberately has no TTL and PITR is on (setup_aws.py:170-194), guarded by a test (test_ledger_iam_policy.py:127-134). Any scheduler-side cleanup, archival, or 'prune old entries' step would need dynamodb:DeleteItem, which is explicitly denied for every principal in the account by scripts/iam_ledger_append_only.json — so such a step cannot be built, and should not be designed.

A re-score MUST NOT write refined_esi_level / refined_confidence / refined_probabilities / refined_conformal_set / refined_top_features / refined_source / refined_at / measured_vitals onto the patient row via storage.update_patient. Those fields are read by routers/patients.py (list :46, detail :101-108) and rendered by frontend/src/components/clinician/PatientCard.tsx:20-21, which displays refined_esi_level in preference to esi_level. Writing them from a shadow scorer displays the shadow score to clinicians, which the programme forbids. The ledger must be the ONLY sink.

A re-score MUST apply services/triage_rules.evaluate() with the raise-only comparison (`shortcut.esi_level < esi_level`, services/triage.py:134) before the score is recorded. triage_ml.predict has no floor of its own and routers/triage.py:61 does not add one, so a scheduler that calls predict() directly reproduces the current unfloored refine-triage behaviour — and HANDOFF.md:547-548 makes the floor a DoD item. Do NOT copy the intake router's unconditional `if shortcut: esi_level = shortcut.esi_level` (routers/intake.py:192-194): that form can lower acuity.

A re-score MUST NOT reuse the existing Lambda handler's scheduled-event branch. backend/main.py:266 already claims every `{"source": "aws.events"}` payload for the warmup path and returns 200 without reaching Mangum. A new EventBridge rule needs either a distinct discriminator checked before that branch, or a separate function.

Any scheduled invocation MUST carry an explicit time budget and MUST be created with async retries = 0 and a bounded max event age. Commit 42abe22 is exactly this failure: an unbounded scheduled invocation hit the 60 s timeout, Lambda's default two async retries turned 360 pings/day into 1,080 minute-long 2 GB invocations, and it never warmed anything. The mitigation that worked was a daemon thread joined with a timeout (main.py:253-258), not deadline checks between steps — because the call that hung was _load() itself and it never returned to be checked.

The scheduler MUST NOT enumerate patients with db.storage.list_patients_for_hospital as it stands. It is not a .scan() (PERF-004 is satisfied) but it has no pagination — backend/db/storage.py:181-187 ignores LastEvaluatedKey — so a department larger than one 1 MB DynamoDB page is silently truncated and the missing patients look like patients who were never in the department. Pagination (and ideally a ProjectionExpression, since the row carries prebrief/scribe/differential/workup text the scorer does not need) is required before 'every patient' is a true statement.

The scheduler MUST measure and record input completeness itself. The model cannot report it: build_row substitutes normal values for every absent vital (gcs_total->15, mental_status->'alert', shock_index->0.8, weight/height/bmi->70/170/24, triage_ml.py:346-351) and the miss_* features are dead at inference because imputation runs before they are computed (triage_ml.py:366-370 vs train_triage_model.py:171-179). A 5-minute cadence over patients with no fresh vitals will therefore score them as if their vitals were normal. The DoD requirement that the model 'refuses to emit below a completeness threshold' has to be implemented outside predict().

A None return from triage_ml.predict MUST be recorded as a distinct refusal/failure event, not skipped. predict() catches every exception and returns None (triage_ml.py:646-648), the same value it returns when artifacts are missing (:592). A scheduler that treats None as 'nothing to write' produces a silent ledger gap, and encounter_ledger.py's own docstring (:102-109) states the gap reads as 'nothing happened to this patient' rather than 'we failed to write it down'.

Every ledger append MUST supply model_version and an uncertainty dict containing a 'coverage' key, or record() raises. Use triage_ml.model_version() (returns (version, source)) and pass result['conformal_coverage'] plus result['conformal_coverage_source'] — the source tag matters because today's artifacts do not record a calibration target, so coverage is the 0.90 placeholder with source 'declared_default' (triage_ml.py:481, :618-620; encounter_ledger.py:288-296, :261-265).

Concurrency MUST be bounded per encounter. encounter_ledger.record serialises on a process-global lock (encounter_ledger.py:299) and, on a cold container, does a ConsistentRead Query of the entire chain before every write (:182-186). Two containers scoring the same encounter contend on the conditional put and retry up to 8 times (:115, :320-329). Fan-out should be per-encounter-exclusive, or the cadence will pay a full chain read plus retries per score.

The re-scorer MUST NOT introduce a new boto3 client in backend/services/. ARCH-002 (L1) confines boto3 to db/; triage_ml.py:45-47 and encounter_ledger.py:124-129 already violate it and a scheduler that adds a third is entrenching the breach. New DynamoDB access belongs in db/storage.py.

The re-scorer MUST NOT route through any module that imports services.transcription, services.tts, lib.claude or services.voice_agent.tts_cache. Staying off those four keeps it outside the SEC-004 derived scope (CONSTITUTION.md:90, tests/services/test_consent_gate.py PROVIDER_LEAVES) and keeps a re-score at pure local CPU cost. triage_ml + triage_rules + encounter_ledger satisfy this today; adding a Claude explanation step to a re-score would pull the whole scheduled path into the consent gate and a per-score provider bill.

Idempotency has a free win and a trap. predict() is deterministic — build_row hard-codes arrival_hour/day/season/shift (triage_ml.py:326-334), so identical inputs give bit-identical outputs and a duplicate trigger cannot produce a different score. But the ledger has no dedupe: record() always allocates a new sequence number, so duplicate triggers append duplicate entries. Dedupe must be decided by the caller (e.g. compare against encounter_ledger.latest(encounter_id, model=...) before writing), and the DoD requirement that a missed cadence be a ledger event means 'no change' may still need an entry.

Long-running containers MUST bound encounter_ledger._entries. It is a module-global dict appended to on every write and populated by read-through on every cold encounter (encounter_ledger.py:90, :213-217, :334), with no eviction outside the test-only reset(). At <=5-minute cadence across a whole department for 90 days it grows monotonically inside a 2 GB function whose model working set already peaks at 642 MB.

The 24-hour patient TTL (db/storage.py:28-29, :104-105) bounds how long the inputs a re-score needs actually exist. Any encounter whose scoring window approaches 24 h loses transcript/medical_info/language from DynamoDB while its ledger entries persist, so the re-scorer must either extend the TTL for enrolled encounters or snapshot the immutable inputs into the ledger at enrolment.

'Currently in the department' is not representable today. The only statuses are 'waiting' and 'seen' (db/constants.py) and nothing marks departure, so the scheduler cannot derive length of stay or know when to stop scoring from the existing data model. A departure/discharge signal has to be added before 'for their whole length of stay' can be implemented or measured.

MUST NOT send a raw EventBridge event to `main.handler`. backend/main.py:266 routes anything with `source == "aws.events"` into the warmup branch, which dry-predicts on a fake patient called "warm" and returns 200. A scheduled re-score wired that way would report success while scoring nobody — the worst possible failure mode for a programme whose only output is a ledger.

MUST NOT send a constant-Input EventBridge payload to `main.handler` either. Without `warmup` or `source` the event falls through to Mangum, which raises RuntimeError (mangum/adapter.py:69-75) because no inferer matches (alb.py:89, api_gateway.py:72, api_gateway.py:138, lambda_at_edge.py:17-20). EventBridge→Lambda is an ASYNC invoke, so that RuntimeError is precisely the retry-amplified error class from 42abe22.

MUST give the scheduler its OWN Lambda function (same ECR image, different CMD/handler). Sharing `solace-api` means sharing one 60s timeout, one memory setting, one async-invoke config, one Errors metric, and one concurrency pool with the clinician-facing API. A separate function costs nothing extra (same image, PAY_PER_REQUEST) and buys: an independent timeout, an alarm that can actually see the scheduler, a reserved-concurrency blast cap, and escape from the PERF-002 dispatch collision without amending CONSTITUTION.md:748-755 or breaking the deploy smoke test at scripts/deploy_container.py:174-184.

MUST set an explicit async retry policy AND a DLQ, and MUST set it in code, not the console. The 3x multiplier in 42abe22 was Lambda's default two async retries. Set it in both places: `RetryPolicy={"MaximumRetryAttempts": 0, "MaximumEventAgeInSeconds": 60}` plus `DeadLetterConfig` on the EventBridge target, and `put_function_event_invoke_config(MaximumRetryAttempts=0, MaximumEventAgeInSeconds=60)` on the function. Today zero of these appear anywhere in the repo, and scripts/deploy_container.py:157-161 actively erases target-level config by calling put_targets with the same Id and no RetryPolicy.

MUST set `ReservedConcurrentExecutions` on the scheduler function (1 or 2). This is the single cheapest hard ceiling on a runaway — it makes over-spend physically impossible rather than merely unlikely — and it converts the already-deployed `solace-lambda-throttles` alarm (setup_cloudwatch_alarms.py:55-61, Sum(Throttles) > 0) into a working runaway detector. Nothing in the repo sets reserved concurrency today.

MUST bound the work inside the handler with the same pattern as backend/main.py:253-257, not with a between-steps deadline check. The commit records that the between-steps version was written first and was useless, because the call that hung never returned to be checked. A tick that scores N patients must check a monotonic deadline derived from `context.get_remaining_time_in_millis()` before starting each patient, AND cap total in-handler work well below the function timeout, AND record the patients it did not reach as ledger gap events (HANDOFF.md:543-545 requires a missed cadence to be a ledger event, not a silent absence).

MUST NOT rely on `dynamodb:BatchWriteItem` for ledger writes. scripts/iam_ledger_append_only.json explicitly Denies it on solace-encounter-ledger for solace-lambda-exec, and an IAM Deny beats every Allow. Every score is an individual conditional PutItem; the cost and latency model must assume one WCU-class write plus one conditional-check per score.

MUST NOT try to parallelise ledger appends inside a single container. backend/services/encounter_ledger.py:299 holds one global `threading.Lock` across the whole of `record()` including the DynamoDB PutItem at :321, so threads or asyncio buy nothing on the write path. Fan-out for throughput must be across invocations, not within one.

MUST fix or bound `_load_all` before running 90 days at a 5-minute cadence. backend/services/encounter_ledger.py:182-187 is an unpaginated Query; once a chain exceeds DynamoDB's 1 MB response the read truncates, seq comes back too low, the conditional PutItem fails, and `record()` raises LedgerUnavailable after `_MAX_SEQ_ATTEMPTS = 8`. A boarding patient at 288 scores/day with SHAP attributions in every entry is a realistic way to reach that. Either paginate, or Query with `ScanIndexForward=False, Limit=1` to read only the tail.

MUST NOT let the in-memory `_entries` cache (encounter_ledger.py:90) grow unbounded in a long-lived scheduler container. A tick job touching every patient in the department will accumulate every chain it has ever seen in a container that Lambda may keep alive for hours.

MUST NOT invoke the scheduler through API Gateway. The HTTP API has a hard 29-second integration timeout that the 60s Lambda timeout does not respect, so a batch triggered over HTTP silently truncates. Invoke Lambda directly from EventBridge.

MUST NOT reuse `POST /patients/{id}/refine-triage` as the scheduled path. backend/routers/triage.py:53-55 requires a clinician via `Depends(require_clinician)` and audits the action against that clinician (`audit(caller, "triage.refine", ...)`). A scheduler has no clinician; attributing 500,000 automated scores to a human would poison the COMP-002 audit trail. The scheduler needs a distinct non-human principal in the audit model, and the shared scoring logic must be lifted into a service that both the router and the scheduler call (ARCH-001).

SHAPE — the cheapest correct AWS shape here is ONE EventBridge schedule -> ONE dedicated Lambda per tick that loops the department in-process, NOT per-patient fan-out. Sizing from HANDOFF.md:783 (BSW McKinney, 43,301 ED visits/year ≈ 119/day; at a 4-6h LOS the average census is ~20-30, peak maybe 50): a per-tick loop is 288 invocations/day, and each pays the catboost/shap/artifacts.pkl load at most once per warm container. Per-patient fan-out is ~6,000-14,000 invocations/day, each risking a cold start that in 42abe22 was measured at 642 MB and 60+ seconds. On a 2048 MB arm64 function the per-tick shape lands in the low single-digit dollars per month; the fan-out shape is roughly an order of magnitude worse for identical output, and its per-invocation cold starts are the exact cost profile that produced the $14.56 bill. This is a two-way door: if the census outgrows one tick, add a shard key to the schedule rather than fanning out per patient.

SHAPE — EventBridge Scheduler is preferable to a classic EventBridge rule, mainly for reasons of evidence rather than price. Both express `rate(5 minutes)`; both can carry a retry policy and a DLQ; per-invocation cost at 288/day is negligible either way. Scheduler wins because retry policy and DLQ are first-class properties of the schedule itself rather than a mix of target config and function-level async config, and because it supports timezone-anchored and one-time schedules (useful for pinning the 90-day window and for the week-14 cutover). The rule wins only on familiarity: scripts/deploy_container.py already speaks `events.put_targets`. Either way the schedule MUST be created in a committed script — the current `solace-warmer` rule exists in no file, which is why its 4-minute cadence and its now-DISABLED state are unauditable.

SHAPE — Step Functions is the wrong tool at this size but the right tool if the loop ever needs per-patient isolation. An Express Map over 20-50 patients per tick adds state-transition billing and a second failure surface for output that one Lambda loop already produces. Revisit only if (a) a single patient's failure must not abort the rest of the tick in a way retry-in-handler cannot express, or (b) the department census grows past what fits in one bounded invocation. Note it also multiplies the ledger's per-item PutItem count without being able to batch (BatchWriteItem is IAM-denied).

SHAPE — in-process asyncio is NOT available on Lambda and MUST NOT be designed for. Lambda freezes the container between invocations (the mechanism backend/main.py:216-218 relies on to stop billing a runaway thread), so a background loop simply does not run. A real event loop means moving off Lambda to Fargate/ECS, which for this workload costs more than the per-tick Lambda shape (an always-on task sized for the ~642 MB ML footprint runs higher than the low single-digit dollars the tick shape needs) while giving up the bounded-invocation property that is the whole safety story from 42abe22. The one thing it would buy is no cold starts.

MUST add alarms that would have caught 42abe22, because the current set demonstrably would not. Minimum: Duration p99 approaching the scheduler's timeout; Invocations above the expected 288/day envelope (a cadence that speeds up is the runaway signature); Errors on the SCHEDULER function specifically with a threshold below its own tick rate — note `solace-lambda-errors` at scripts/setup_cloudwatch_alarms.py:48-54 fires only above 5 errors per 5 minutes, and the incident ran at roughly 3.75, which is why it went undetected for weeks; a DLQ-depth alarm; and an AWS Budgets / EstimatedCharges alarm, of which the repo has none.

MUST add `solace-encounter-ledger` to the DynamoDB alarm set AND fix the metric. scripts/setup_cloudwatch_alarms.py:73-80 alarms on `UserErrors` dimensioned by TableName, but UserErrors is an account-level aggregate with no TableName dimension — with `TreatMissingData="notBreaching"` those ten alarms sit permanently OK on no data. Use ThrottledRequests / ReadThrottleEvents / WriteThrottleEvents, and include the ledger table, which is currently absent from the list entirely.

MUST make the 90-day cadence self-limiting. The 42abe22 warmer ran unnoticed for weeks because nothing could stop it except a human noticing an invoice. A shadow programme with a stated end date should carry that date in the schedule (an EventBridge Scheduler end-date, or a hard kill in the handler) so the programme cannot outlive its own window by accident.

MUST keep re-scoring idempotent per (encounter, tick). A duplicate EventBridge delivery — which is at-least-once, not exactly-once — must not append a second ledger entry for the same observation window. The conditional PutItem at encounter_ledger.py:165-168 protects sequence integrity but not semantic duplication; seq is allocated from `len(chain) + 1`, so a duplicate tick appends a legitimately-numbered duplicate score and inflates the week-14 denominators.

MUST express all of this in a committed, re-runnable script alongside the existing scripts/*.py, and MUST assert it in a test the way test_warmup_is_bounded.py asserts the warmup budget. The lasting lesson of 42abe22 is not the matplotlib bug — it is that two of the four fixes live only in the console, so nothing can prove today that retries are still 0 or that the warmer is still disabled.

The scheduled re-score MUST NOT be delivered as a plain EventBridge event to the existing solace-api Lambda handler. backend/main.py:266 short-circuits on `event.get("source") == "aws.events"` and returns a 200 warmup body without dispatching. PERF-002 (L1) requires that branch to exist, so it cannot be removed. Either (a) use a separate function with its own handler, or (b) discriminate on a field the warmup branch does not consume and reorder the checks so the re-score branch is tested FIRST — and add a test that asserts a re-score event does not return {"warm": true}, because that failure is silent and reports success.

Whatever function receives the schedule MUST have its async invoke config pinned to MaximumRetryAttempts=0 and a short MaximumEventAge IN CODE, in scripts/deploy_container.py (or an equivalent script), not by hand in the console. The current script deletes and recreates the function on every deploy and never sets EventInvokeConfig, so the exact retry amplification from 42abe22 (360 pings -> 1,080 invocations) returns on the next deploy. This is the specific way this project has already lost money once.

The re-score path MUST carry a hard time budget of the same shape as _run_warmup: work on a joined thread with a timeout, not a deadline checked between steps. 42abe22 records that the between-steps version was tried first and was useless, because the call that hung was _load() and it never returned to be checked (backend/main.py:208-222, backend/tests/test_warmup_is_bounded.py:49-65). A per-patient budget AND a per-invocation budget are both needed, since the loop length is the department census.

The job MUST NOT call storage.update_patient / storage.put_patient with any scoring field. refined_esi_level is projected by routers/patients.py:46-48,101-107 and PatientCard.tsx:20-22 displays it in preference to esi_level. Writing the patient row is writing the ED board. The ledger is the only write target the shadow guarantee permits.

The job MUST NOT call services.workflows.engine.fire(). One call reaches send_sms, send_slack_webhook, http_webhook, create_clinician_note, set_patient_field, ehr_write and notify (services/workflows/actions.py:375-520). refine_triage does call fire() at routers/triage.py:121-136, so the shadow scorer must not be built by copying refine_triage's body.

The job MUST NOT expose a route. SEC-003's scope is 'derived from the route table — any handler with no auth dependency' (CONSTITUTION.md:71); adding a shadow read endpoint would pull it into SEC-003 and into the public surface. During the 90 days the ledger's existing reader endpoints (routers/encounters.py:56, :83) are clinician-authenticated and would surface a shadow score to a clinician on request — either shadow encounters must be excluded from them or those routes must be off for the shadow cohort.

Iteration MUST be per-hospital and driven by an explicit hospital_id, via storage.list_patients_for_hospital(hospital_id, ...). There is no cross-tenant enumeration primitive today and none must be added; a `list_all_patients` helper would create the SEC-008 violation that does not currently exist. Every ledger write must be preceded by a tenancy check on the loaded row (tenancy.belongs_to(row, hospital_id), lib/tenancy.py:62-71) rather than trusting the GSI query.

Iteration MUST paginate. _ddb_query_patients_by_hospital (db/storage.py:181-187) does not handle LastEvaluatedKey. Silently scoring only the first 1 MB page of a department is a correctness failure that the week-14 under-triage number would absorb without any error surfacing.

The ledger entry MUST carry hospital_id, or the week-14 analysis cannot scope its own evidence. Today the item has no tenant column (encounter_ledger.py:148-163) and the table has no GSI (setup_aws.py:170-180), while tenancy on the read path is borrowed from a patient row that is TTL'd 30 minutes after the patient is marked seen (routers/patients.py:190-200). Adding hospital_id to the item changes the hash payload in _digest (encounter_ledger.py:234-249) and therefore breaks verification of any chain written before the change — so it must be decided BEFORE the programme starts, not during it.

The programme MUST retain an enumerable index of its own encounter_ids outside the patients table. The ledger allow grants PutItem/GetItem/Query only, no Scan (scripts/iam_ledger_allow.json), and the ledger has no GSI, so at week 14 there is no way to ask 'which encounters exist'. Widening the IAM allow to add Scan would trip test_ledger_iam_policy.py:110-115.

A ledger write failure MUST NOT be swallowed. routers/triage.py:114-118 catches LedgerUnavailable and continues, correctly, because the score is already in front of the clinician. In the shadow programme the ledger entry IS the entire product, so the failure must be surfaced and counted (the audit module's _write_failures + /health pattern at lib/audit.py:41-50 and main.py:100-110 is the in-repo precedent), not logged and dropped.

Every ledger entry MUST carry an uncertainty dict containing a 'coverage' key or the write raises MissingUncertainty (encounter_ledger.py:253-265), and MUST carry a model_version, obtained from triage_ml.model_version() which also reports whether the version was declared or content-hashed (triage_ml.py:552-586). observed_at must be timezone-aware or record() raises (encounter_ledger.py:292-296).

Audit writes from the job MUST be synchronous, or explicitly drained before the handler returns. lib/audit.py:156-160 dispatches to the default asyncio executor and returns; Lambda freezes the container the instant the handler returns, so queued audit rows are lost with no error. The job should call the synchronous path or await completion.
Audit action names MUST NOT begin with 'abuse.' unless abuse is meant. lib/audit.py:170-184 auto-increments the blocklist for any action with that prefix.

The job MUST log neither patient identifiers nor clinical content. lib/log_redaction.py only redacts hyphenated UUID4, 'Bearer <tok>' and 'intake_token=<tok>' — not pt-<hex> ids, names, complaints, vitals or ESI values. If the scheduler runs as a separate entrypoint it MUST call log_redaction.install() as its first act, since backend/main.py:34 is the only thing that installs it today and a handler that does not import main gets nothing. Follow the audit.py:83-90 pattern: log the action and the count, never the item.

Whether a consent gate is required MUST be decided explicitly and written down, because neither SEC-004's derived scope nor its test reaches this path (triage_ml is outside the provider closure; the rule only obliges unauthenticated ROUTES). If the answer is 'yes', the mechanism already exists: consent.for_patient(patient) at lib/consent.py:89-98, gated once at a single choke point in the scorer with a test that calls it and asserts refusal — the services.workflows.actions.run pattern (test_consent_gate.py:62-64, :407-419), not a per-call-site check.

The job MUST NOT reach any of the four provider leaves (services.transcription, services.tts, lib.claude, services.voice_agent.tts_cache). Doing so would pull it into SEC-004's derived scope, and would additionally engage SEC-005 (L1, content_guard.scan before submission), COMP-001 (L1, Safe Harbor redaction) and COMP-005 (L1, BAA-covered provider — the deployed function currently ships CLAUDE_PROVIDER=direct, scripts/deploy_container.py:111).

Model loading MUST go through triage_ml._load() and its @lru_cache(maxsize=1). PERF-001 (L1) and ARCH-004 (L2) both require it, and the warmup path depends on it being the same cached load (CONSTITUTION.md:737-746, 351-360). A per-invocation model load in a 5-minute loop is also the cost shape that caused the original incident.

Any boto3 the job needs MUST live in db/, per ARCH-002 (L1, CONSTITUTION.md:328-334). services/ already violates this in eleven places including encounter_ledger.py:125-129 — the design should not add a twelfth by putting the scheduler's persistence in services/.

The shadow guarantee MUST be enforced by a derived-scope test whose allowlist is EMPTY, not by review. The product promise is 'no code path exists', so any entry in an ALLOWED_EGRESS dict is the promise being weakened and must be defended in writing — mirroring ALLOWED_UNGATED (test_consent_gate.py:74-109) and ALLOWED_UNTHROTTLED (test_public_endpoint_throttling.py:63-75), each paired with a staleness test and a floor assertion so a scan that matches nothing cannot pass vacuously (test_consent_gate.py:211-219).
all_unknowns: Whether the solace-warmer EventBridge rule is actually disabled in the live account right now. Commit 42abe22 says it was disabled by hand; no code asserts or re-asserts it, and scripts/deploy_container.py:157-171 `point_warmer()` unconditionally re-attaches the target and the lambda:InvokeFunction permission on every deploy. I could not determine live rule state from the repo.
The live async retry configuration on the solace Lambda. It is not in the repo at all, so I cannot confirm retries are still 0 or whether an intervening deploy already reset them.

Actual applied TTL state per table in the live account. The setup scripts are create-if-absent and several return early when the table exists, so the code shows intent, not the deployed configuration.

Real patient item size in bytes and typical concurrent patient count per hospital. Without these I cannot say whether the unpaginated 1MB query at storage.py:182 is already truncating in production or only would at ED scale. This is measurable with a single describe/scan-count against the live table and should be measured before sizing anything.

Whether the live solace-appointments table has confirmation_code-index. setup_aws.py:140-158 and setup_voice_tables.py:124-138 disagree and each no-ops if the table exists, so which GSIs exist depends on run order. db/storage.py:253 queries that index by name and would throw ValidationException if it is absent.

What actually changes between re-scores. `measured_vitals` is a single overwritten field updated only by the nurse-triggered refine-triage route (triage.py:76), and I found no vitals time-series, no EHR polling loop, and no observation feed. Whether a 5-minute cadence has any new input to score is a design question I could not answer from storage alone — it may belong to the EHR-integration area rather than this one.

Whether an ADT / EHR feed exists that could supply a real arrival and discharge signal. backend/routers/ehr.py, ehr_auth.py, services/hl7_v2.py and services/tefca_qhin.py all exist but I did not read them; if one carries ADT events it would be a better source of 'currently in the department' than anything in solace-patients. Worth a targeted look before committing to a GSI design.

The IAM policy attached to the Lambda execution role for solace-patients. scripts/apply_iam_scoped.py produced no matches for dynamodb: actions in my grep, and scripts/iam_solace_developer_policy.json:10 covers `table/solace-*/index/*` but that is the developer policy, not the runtime role. Whether the runtime role can query a NEW index on solace-patients is unverified.

Whether scripts/setup_aws.py has ever actually been run against account 704229156617 — i.e. whether the solace-encounter-ledger table physically EXISTS today. The code is correct and the table definition is right, but nothing in the repo proves the create_table call was executed. If it was not, every production write is failing with ResourceNotFoundException, wrapped as LedgerUnavailable at encounter_ledger.py:331, caught and swallowed by both callers, and visible only as a log line. This is checkable in one command (`aws dynamodb describe-table --table-name solace-encounter-ledger`) and should be the first thing verified.

Whether scripts/enforce_ledger_immutability.py has actually been applied to the live solace-lambda-exec role. If the allow policy (PutItem/GetItem/Query) was never attached, the Lambda cannot write a single ledger row — and test_ledger_iam_policy.py:96-99 explicitly documents that this exact failure already happened once ('the policy simulator said implicitDeny on PutItem while the script printed success').

Whether ANY ledger rows exist in production today. Both write sites are on clinician-triggered paths (refine-triage, ai-override); if neither has been exercised since commit 860d1b3, the durable path has never run even once in the real environment.

The real item size of a triage_ml entry, and therefore the actual entries-per-encounter ceiling before the 1MB Query page truncates. It depends on the serialized size of `top_features` (SHAP output) and `probabilities`, which I did not measure. This determines whether the pagination bug bites at ~300 entries or ~3000, i.e. whether it is a day-two problem or a week-two problem.

Whether CMK_ARN is set when setup_aws.py runs. scripts/setup_aws.py:57-62 only attaches the solace CMK `if CMK_ARN` — so whether the ledger table satisfies COMP-003 (L1, encryption at rest with alias/solace) depends on runtime environment I cannot inspect from the code.

Whether the deployed Lambda is currently the container-image function created by scripts/deploy_container.py (which sets SOLACE_MODE=aws at :103) or something else. I verified the deploy script's intent, not the live function configuration.

Whether DynamoDB actually accepts `attribute_not_exists(encounter_id) AND attribute_not_exists(seq)` as written on this composite-key table. It should — the condition is evaluated against the item at the exact primary key — but no test and no recorded live run exercises it, and test_encounter_ledger_durability.py:22 documents a DIFFERENT expression (`attribute_not_exists(seq)` alone) than the code uses, so the two have drifted and neither has been observed working.

What 'the team recognised at T' will be read from. Nothing in the ledger write path today produces recognition-delay labels; HANDOFF.md:679-681 files it as unbuilt P1-5. Whether those labels are meant to land in this ledger as `model="event"` entries or in a separate store changes the write-path volume estimate substantially.

Actual _load() wall-clock time on a cold start. Not measurable here: backend/models/ contains only .gitkeep (no artifacts.pkl, no fold files anywhere on this filesystem), and the local .venv has no numpy/pandas/lightgbm/xgboost/catboost/shap installed. The only hard evidence is indirect: the 42abe22 report shows a warmup exceeding 60 s when matplotlib's font cache had to be rebuilt, and WARMUP_BUDGET_SECONDS = 20.0 was chosen as the ceiling afterwards — which implies the healthy load was believed to fit inside 20 s, not that it was measured at some value.

Actual artifact size on disk. scripts/train_triage_model.py:564-567 prints a total_mb figure at training time but no artifact exists here to measure and no size is recorded in the repo. Shape is known (1 pickle containing 2 TF-IDF vectorizers, label encoders, 5 MLP models + 5 scalers, meta-learner, thresholds; plus up to 15 fold .txt files) but not its bytes.

Per-prediction latency. Not measurable without artifacts. The composition is knowable — 2 TF-IDF transforms, ~5 lgbm + 5 xgb + 5 cat + 5 MLP forward passes on one row, one meta-learner call, and one extra LightGBM pred_contrib pass for SHAP — but there is no benchmark, test, or recorded number anywhere in the repo.

Whether the currently deployed image actually contains artifacts.pkl. buildspec.yml treats the S3 copy as best-effort ('|| echo WARN artifacts.pkl missing -> ensemble stays disabled'), so the deployed function may be running the clinical_simulation fallback. GET /health reports which (backend/main.py:108 `"triage": "trained_ensemble" if _triage_models_present() else "clinical_simulation"`), but that requires calling the live endpoint.

Whether the solace-encounter-ledger DynamoDB table exists and with what key schema. LEDGER_TABLE is named at encounter_ledger.py:57 and scripts/enforce_ledger_immutability.py + tests/test_ledger_iam_policy.py exist, but the module docstring (:29-32) says 'Storage is in-memory here. The DynamoDB backing ... is deliberately not written yet', which contradicts the _persist/_load_all implementation present in the file. Which statement reflects deployed reality is not determinable from the code.

Where continuous vitals would come from. Nothing in the repo ingests a vitals feed — no FHIR Observation poller, no device stream, no HL7 ORU path writing vitals to a patient row. routers/care_ops.py:285 accepts a `vitals: list[dict]` for a FHIR write-back and services/ehr_copilot.py:79 reads `patient.get("vitals")`, a key nothing ever writes. Without a feed, a 5-minute cadence re-scores identical inputs and produces identical scores.

Whether art['conformal_coverage'] will exist after the next retrain. The code path for a calibrated coverage figure exists (triage_ml.py:618-620) but the training script does not write the key, and there is no open item in the repo that says it will.

Typical department census at the pilot site, which determines whether the missing pagination in _ddb_query_patients_by_hospital is a latent bug or an immediate one, and how many predicts must fit in a 60 s Lambda per cycle.

Whether the disabled solace-warmer EventBridge rule was ever re-enabled after 42abe22 disabled it, and whether the retries=0 / max-event-age settings described in that commit message were applied to the function itself or only to that rule. Neither is expressed in any file in this repo — the commit message is the only record.

Which of the three shortcut-application semantics is clinically intended (raise-only at services/triage.py:134, unconditional at routers/intake.py:192, absent at routers/triage.py). The repo documents the raise-only rule as the invariant (CONSTITUTION-adjacent prose in services/model_cards.py:164 and HANDOFF.md:547-548) but two of the three call sites do not implement it.

The `solace-warmer` rule's actual schedule expression and current state. The commit says it was DISABLED and the 4-minute cadence is inferred from the commit text (360/day = 1440/4), but no file in the repo contains a ScheduleExpression. It cannot be verified from code that it is still disabled.

Whether the async-invoke config from 42abe22 (MaximumRetryAttempts=0, MaximumEventAgeInSeconds=60) is currently applied to `solace-api`. It appears in no script and no test. It would be wiped by the delete/recreate branch at scripts/deploy_container.py:85-90.

Whether `scripts/setup_cloudwatch_alarms.py` has ever been run against the account, whether the SNS email subscription to solace-security-alerts was ever confirmed, and therefore whether the Errors alarm was even armed during the incident.

Whether provisioned concurrency is currently active. scripts/enable_provisioned.py:144 sets PC=1 on alias `live`, while scripts/deploy_container.py:23 says `ALIAS = None  # unused — we put LIVE function on $LATEST`. The two scripts contradict each other and the 42abe22 cost breakdown does not mention PC at all.

The commit's arithmetic does not reconcile with published pricing and I could not resolve it from the repo. 1,080 invocations/day x 63.353s billed x 2 GB ≈ 137,000 GB-s/day ≈ 4.1M GB-s over 30 days, which at arm64 rates is roughly $55, not the $14.56 stated. The likeliest explanation is that the failure did not span the full 30-day billing window ("for weeks"), but nothing in the repo establishes when it started.

Actual wall-clock cost of one `triage_ml.predict()` call on a warm 2048 MB arm64 container. No benchmark, no timing test, and no CloudWatch duration figure for a successful invocation exists in the repo — the only measured duration on record is the 60s timeout. Without it, the per-tick budget for N patients cannot be sized, only bounded.

Actual serialised size of one ledger Entry in DynamoDB, which determines how many entries fit under the 1 MB Query limit and therefore when the unpaginated `_load_all` starts truncating. The `top_features` SHAP payload is the dominant unknown.

Whether `solace-encounter-ledger` writes are actually exercised in production today. HANDOFF.md:495 says the ledger is "Exists in-memory ... Durable backing **unverified**", and encounter_ledger.py:29-33 still carries a docstring claiming "Storage is in-memory here. The DynamoDB backing ... is deliberately not written yet", which the code at :132-187 contradicts.

CodeBuild's compute architecture. buildspec.yml:42 builds without `--platform linux/arm64` and then update-function-code's an arm64 function. Whether that works depends on the CodeBuild image, which is configured outside the repo.
What triggers the CodeBuild project (webhook, branch filter, manual). buildspec.yml exists but nothing in the repo defines the project or its source trigger.

How "currently in the department" would be determined. `list_patients_for_hospital` accepts a `status` filter (backend/db/storage.py:128) but the AWS path `_ddb_query_patients_by_hospital` (:181-187) queries the GSI by hospital_id with no status condition and no pagination, so the tick's enumeration cost and correctness depend on a status model I did not trace.
Whether the account has any AWS Budgets or Cost Anomaly Detection configured. None appears in the repo; the 42abe22 discovery was evidently manual invoice review.

THE SHADOW GUARANTEE TEST — concrete design, since this is the deliverable the brief asked for and it does not exist yet. Proposed file: backend/tests/test_shadow_has_no_egress.py, rule SHADOW-001 (L1). (1) DERIVE THE EGRESS LEAVES rather than listing them, using the docstring-blanking trick from test_consent_gate.py:221-241: ast.parse every first-party module, blank every ast.Expr/ast.Constant string so prose cannot match, ast.unparse, and match call signatures for each egress mechanism — HTTP response (any FunctionDef carrying an ast.Call decorator whose func is an ast.Attribute in {get,post,put,patch,delete}, i.e. SEC-003's exact route detector at test_public_endpoint_throttling.py:87-91); patient-row writes ('storage.update_patient(', 'storage.put_patient('); notes ('storage.add_note('); messaging ('sms.send(', 'send_email(', 'boto3.client(\"sns'); webhooks ('httpx.', 'requests.'); EHR write-back ('services.fhir_writer', 'services.ehr_gateway', 'services.hl7_v2', 'ehr_writeback_queue'); and the workflow fan-out ('workflows.engine.fire(', 'engine.fire(') — fire() is a single leaf standing for seven actions (services/workflows/actions.py:375-520). Assert the derived leaf set is a superset of a small hand floor so a broken matcher cannot pass empty, and assert no NEW module matches an egress signature without being declared, exactly as test_provider_leaves_are_still_the_only_leaves does. (2) COMPUTE THE SHADOW CLOSURE by running the SEC-004 fixed point FORWARD from one declared root: build the same edges map as test_consent_gate.py:118-142 (_source_modules + _import_edges), seed reachable={'services.shadow_scorer'}, and repeatedly add every first-party dep of every member until stable. (3) ASSERT reachable ∩ EGRESS_LEAVES == set(), with ALLOWED_EGRESS: dict[str,str] keyed 'module:leaf' whose correct steady state is EMPTY, plus a test_exemptions_still_correspond_to_real_edges killing stale entries. (4) ASSERT THE WRITE ALLOWLIST — closure proves unreachability, not that the writes it does make are the right ones. AST-walk the shadow package for every attribute call and assert the set of qualified callee names ⊆ {encounter_ledger.record, audit.record, storage.get_patient, storage.list_patients_for_hospital, triage_ml.predict, triage_ml.model_version, consent.for_patient, tenancy.belongs_to} — read-only on the patient store, append-only on the ledger. This is the assertion that catches the specific trap that writing refined_esi_level is writing the ED board. (5) ASSERT NO ROUTE: no FunctionDef in the shadow package carries a verb decorator, and main.py contains no include_router for the shadow package. (6) DRIVE IT, because both existing derived-scope tests do and the preamble says a cited line proves nothing: in local mode, seed one patient, monkeypatch spies onto storage.update_patient, storage.put_patient, storage.add_note, sms.send, email.send_email, httpx.Client.post, workflows.engine.fire and lib.claude.messages_create, run exactly one scoring pass, assert every spy has zero calls, and assert encounter_ledger.timeline(pid) gained exactly one entry with verify(pid).ok is True. (7) FLOOR ASSERTIONS on len(SHADOW_MODULES) and on the leaf set. I could not implement or verify this because the scorer module does not exist yet — the root name is the one thing the design must fix before the test can be written.

The legal basis for the shadow programme — treatment and operations, quality improvement, or research under IRB — is not determinable from the code, and it decides whether a consent gate is required at all. The constitution defers the structurally identical voice question to the deploying hospital's counsel (CONSTITUTION.md:108-111) and ships VOICE_CONSENT_MODE as a setting rather than picking an answer. The same shape is probably right here, but the code cannot answer it.

How patients enter the system for the shadow programme is entirely unspecified in code. routers/intake.py:302 is the only caller of storage.put_patient, so today a patient row exists only if that patient completed Solace's own intake. 'Re-score EVERY patient currently in the department' implies an EHR-driven census that has no ingestion path, no consent_granted_at, and therefore no row for consent.for_patient() to read. I could not determine whether the design intends to create shadow patient rows, to key the ledger off an EHR encounter id instead, or something else — and this choice determines almost every other answer above.

Whether the solace-warmer EventBridge rule is currently enabled or disabled in AWS. 42abe22 says it was disabled, but that state lives only in AWS; scripts/deploy_container.py:157-171 re-points it on every deploy regardless. I ran no AWS calls (read-only investigation, no credentials used).

The actual size of the patient set per hospital, so I cannot say whether the un-paginated GSI query in _ddb_query_patients_by_hospital would exceed the 1 MB page today. The defect is real regardless; only its current blast radius is unknown.

Whether triage_ml.predict() is safe to call repeatedly on a patient with no measured vitals. refine_triage requires a VitalsBody and raises 400 when body is None (routers/triage.py:57-58), and the warmup path constructs a full synthetic vitals dict (main.py:236-246). A continuous re-scorer over a whole department will frequently have partial or absent vitals, and I did not read predict()'s imputation behaviour far enough to say what it returns or whether the conformal coverage figure remains meaningful under heavy missingness. The strategy doc's own acceptance bar says the estimate must 'refuse to emit when input completeness is below a stated threshold' (docs/strategy/2026-07-30-product-strategy.md:302), and I found no such threshold in the code.

Whether the S3 audit archive is actually configured in production. lib/audit.py:99-100 silently returns without archiving when solace_mode != 'aws' or s3_bucket_media is unset, which would leave only the 90-day DynamoDB TTL against COMP-002's 6-year requirement. Determining this needs AWS access.

Whether adding hospital_id to the ledger item is acceptable mid-flight. It enters _digest's payload (encounter_ledger.py:234-249), so every pre-existing chain would fail verify() after the change. I could not determine whether any production ledger entries exist yet.
